title: Workspace switch block on unsaved changes offers no explicit save/discard choice
body:
## Context

Static review of `main` (`db806b4`). This is a UX/product-boundary issue, not a rare crash path.

The workflow shell blocks workspace switching whenever the current workspace reports a dirty or in-flight state, but the user is only told "finish the work first" — there is no explicit choice between "stay and save" and "leave without saving". For a tool that edits a physical-room document, silently forcing the user to preserve every unsaved edit is a stronger contract than the UI admits.

## Evidence

- `backend/src/htdt/workflow_shell.py` ~L132-153: `WorkspaceRouter.navigate` runs `current.before_deactivate()`; a `False` return blocks the switch entirely and only surfaces `last_block_reason` in the status bar.
- `backend/src/htdt/room_workspace.py` ~L246-253: `before_deactivate` returns `False` for `working.is_dirty`, `has_preview`, or `recovery_candidate`, with reasons like "未保存の変更を保存または元に戻してから画面を切り替えてください".
- `backend/src/htdt/room_workspace.py` ~L1718-1725: `save()` persists the current working document as a new `SceneRevision`. There is no corresponding discard/revert action offered to the user inside the blocked navigation.
- `workflow_application.py` binds `project.save` globally (Ctrl+S) to the active workspace's save, so the only supported exit from a dirty state is "save now" or manually undo every edit.

## Why it matters

1. A user who made a wrong edit and wants to switch to another workspace is trapped: they cannot leave without either committing the edit as a new immutable revision or manually undoing it. That makes exploration risky and penalizes experimentation.
2. The UI presents the block as a generic "finish your work" notice, not as an explicit save/discard decision. The product boundary between "keep the draft" and "abandon the draft" is invisible.
3. This is the kind of usability/spec inconsistency the product keeps running into: the underlying model has a clean save/discard distinction, but the workflow surface only exposes the save half.

## Suggestion

When `before_deactivate` returns `False` because of unsaved changes, offer an explicit two-path choice — e.g. a small confirmation sheet with "Save and switch" vs "Discard changes and switch" (and a cancel). If the product intentionally forbids discard, the block reason should say so explicitly instead of implying the user can "元に戻す" (which is currently not a first-class action on the blocked path).

Project field labels: printable QR/short IDs for exact equipment instances, cable runs and terminations
body:
## Summary

Cross-product equipment/commissioning review found a useful missing bridge between:

- HTDT InstalledEquipmentInstance / project identity;
- rack/cable installation output;
- HTDT-Capture label scanning and field inventory.

Capture #345/#402 can use OCR/QR/barcode to suggest manufacturer/model/serial candidates.

That is appropriate for manufacturer labels.

But HTDT has no project-owned field label format for a different question:

> Is this exact physical item/cable/termination the same project instance that HTDT means by “Amp 2”, “AVR”, “FL cable”, or “Projector”?

Manufacturer serial/model recognition helps identify the product, but does not necessarily identify:

- the HTDT installed-instance record;
- rack slot;
- cable run;
- termination;
- project role;
- commissioning history.

A small project-generated QR/short-code label can make repeated field work much less ambiguous.

## Goal

Add optional **HTDT Project Identity Labels** for exact project-scoped physical instances and installation endpoints.

This is not enterprise asset management.

The label is only a durable field shortcut to exact HTDT project authority.

## 1. Supported label targets

Initial bounded targets:

- InstalledEquipmentInstance;
- rack/cabinet;
- cable run;
- cable endpoint / wall plate;
- projector/screen mounting reference where useful;
- optionally speaker physical instance.

Do not generate labels for every abstract authority.

## 2. Label payload

Use a versioned compact payload.

Conceptually:

```text
htdt-label-v1
project identity/ref
target kind
stable target ID
label generation/version
optional checksum/signature
```

Normal QR must not contain:
- local filesystem path;
- secrets;
- full project data;
- private notes.

Human-readable fallback:

```text
HTDT
AMP-02
Rack A · U10–U12
```

A short code should be visible even if QR scanning fails.

## 3. Project identity semantics

Compose with #607.

A label belongs to one exact project lineage.

If project is duplicated as a new independent project:
- old labels still identify the source project;
- clone must issue new labels if desired.

Do not silently reinterpret an old printed QR as the clone's instance.

Supported disaster restore/move that retains project identity may retain label meaning.

## 4. Instance identity

Compose with #569.

Label identifies the physical installed-instance authority, not merely EquipmentDefinition.

Example:

Two identical amplifiers have:
- same EquipmentDefinition;
- different InstalledEquipmentInstance IDs;
- different labels.

Scanning the code should distinguish Amp 1 from Amp 2.

## 5. Manufacturer identity remains separate

A project label does not replace:
- serial number;
- manufacturer QR/barcode;
- catalog/model recognition.

Capture may show:

```text
HTDT identity
Amp 2 · Rack A

Manufacturer identity
Buckeye ... · Serial ...
```

Conflicts are surfaced.

Do not overwrite one with the other.

## 6. Capture scan semantics

Capture should recognize HTDT's own label namespace separately from generic QR/barcode.

Flow:

1. scan QR;
2. validate payload/version;
3. match exact Mission/project context where available;
4. show human target;
5. operator confirms physical association;
6. record field observation/evidence.

Scanning a valid code is strong identity evidence for the printed label, but still not proof that the label was attached to the correct device.

Keep operator confirmation/evidence semantics.

## 7. Wrong-project handling

If Capture is executing Mission for Project B and scans label for Project A:

> This label belongs to another HTDT project.

Offer:
- cancel;
- record as unexpected field item where workflow supports it.

Do not map by equipment model/name.

## 8. Missing/stale target

A label may outlive:
- project deletion;
- removed equipment;
- replaced cable.

If target is historical:
- show historical/retired state;
- do not bind automatically to the new replacement.

A replacement can receive a new label.

Do not

title: Capture Mission baseline drift: reconcile returned field evidence against the issuing design before applying it to current state
body:
## Summary

Cross-product field-loop review found an important lifecycle gap between:

- HTDT Mission production (#563);
- Capture Mission supersession/inbox (#386);
- Capture as-built verification (#293);
- HTDT Capture Inbox (#589).

A Mission is issued from an exact HTDT project/design state.

But field work is asynchronous.

Normal workflow:

```text
HTDT Scene R20
-> issue Mission M1
-> user leaves for field work

Meanwhile on desktop:
R20 -> R21 -> R22

Capture completes M1
-> returns evidence originally requested against R20
```

The returned evidence may be perfectly valid.

What is no longer safe is to interpret it as if it was requested against/currently describes R22.

#386 handles a newer Mission explicitly superseding an older Mission.

This issue is different:

> the Mission itself may still be exact and valid, while the current HTDT project has moved beyond its baseline.

#589 mentions compatibility with current project/current Scene, but no dedicated baseline-drift/rebase contract was found.

## Why this matters

Examples:

### Speaker verification

M1 asks to verify FL planned position from R20.

Before return, R22 moves FL by 100 mm.

Capture observes the physical installation corresponding to the old plan.

On return HTDT must not report:
> FL is 100 mm out of tolerance

without first acknowledging that the Mission baseline and current design differ.

### Equipment identity

M1 asks for projector serial/model under R20.

R22 changes only seat geometry.

The returned projector identity may still be fully applicable to current project.

### Room dimension

M1 requests ceiling height.

R22 changes a target curve only.

The returned physical observation is likely still usable.

### Planned target deleted

M1 asks for a surround speaker planned in R20.

R22 removes that speaker from current design.

The observation remains historical field evidence but should not be automatically promoted to the current intended topology.

Therefore the solution cannot be:
> any Scene change makes the whole Mission stale.

It needs typed dependency-aware reconciliation.

## Goal

Add an exact **Mission Baseline Drift / Return Reconciliation** contract.

Every Mission should bind the exact HTDT design/reference authority it was generated from.

On return, HTDT compares:

```text
Mission baseline
vs
current project authority
```

and determines per requirement/result whether the returned evidence is:

- directly applicable;
- historically valid but not current;
- requires reconciliation/rebase;
- conflicts with current design;
- unaffected by the design drift.

Never silently rebind returned evidence to “latest”.

## 1. Mission baseline manifest

#563 Mission producer should include an exact baseline manifest.

Conceptually:

```text
MissionBaseline
- project/document identity
- SceneRevision ID/hash
- selected SystemVariant/current topology refs where relevant
- design checkpoint/ref where useful
- task-specific dependency refs
- generated_at
```

Do not include every project authority indiscriminately.

The baseline should pin only exact authority needed to interpret Mission intent.

## 2. Task-level dependency scope

Each Mission requirement should state what baseline authority it depends on.

Examples:

### Verify speaker placement
Depends on:
- target entity identity;
- exact planned pose;
- field datum/alignment;
- tolerance policy.

### Capture equipment serial
Depends on:
- intended physical entity/equipment slot identity;
- not necessarily exact speaker coordinates.

### Measure room height
Depends on:
- target room/surface identity;
- datum/reference semantics;
- not current target curve or DSP plan.

### Capture listening-position evidence
May depend on:
- exact listener/seat target;
- exact Scene geometry.

This enables precise drift classification.

Do not use one Mission-wide stale boolean.

## 3. Return-time baseline comparison

When a Capture delivery arrives:

1. resolve exact Mission;
2. resolve exact issuing base

title: Representative project performance budget: keep mature HTDT projects responsive as revisions, assets and evidence accumulate
Descriptive Undo/Redo: show what Ctrl+Z will change and expose a bounded working-edit history
body:
## Summary

Deep Room-CAD usability review of HTDT `main@db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb` found that Undo/Redo semantics are structurally present but have almost no user-facing meaning.

Current `cad_document.py` has a useful in-memory command model:

- `MoveEntityCommand`;
- `RotateEntityCommand`;
- `TransformEntitiesCommand`;
- `AddEntitiesCommand`;
- `ReplaceEntityCommand`;
- `DeleteEntityCommand`;
- `ReplaceDocumentCommand`;
- `CommandHistory`.

But `EditCommand` exposes only `is_noop`, `apply`, and `revert`.

There is no canonical human description such as:

- Move Front Left speaker;
- Rotate projector;
- Change screen size;
- Add 4 seats;
- Delete rack;
- Edit room outline.

The UI therefore cannot answer the basic CAD question:

> What exactly will Ctrl+Z undo?

As Room editing grows to include multi-select, rich geometry, constraints, treatments, attachments and installation geometry, generic unlabelled Undo becomes increasingly risky.

This issue is separate from #485 SceneRevision history.

## Goal

Add a bounded **Editing History / Descriptive Undo** contract for the active working document.

Immediate target:

```text
Undo Move Front Left
Redo Change screen height
```

with an optional short recent-action list.

Do not turn mouse movement into a persistent project audit log.

## 1. Keep three histories separate

### Edit Command History

- current working document/session;
- reversible;
- ephemeral;
- Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y;
- this issue.

### SceneRevision History #485

- immutable saved project history;
- persists across sessions;
- compare/restore by creating new authority.

### Project Lifecycle Timeline #615

- significant cross-workspace events;
- not an Undo stack.

Do not merge them.

## 2. Command presentation contract

Extend command semantics with presentation metadata or a separate describer.

Conceptually:

```text
EditCommandPresentation
- action_kind
- primary_subject_name
- subject_count
- optional property/summary
- localized label key
```

Examples:

```text
Move “Front Left”
Rotate 3 speakers
Change “Screen” dimensions
Add 4 seats
Delete “Projector”
Edit room outline
```

Do not persist localized prose as command authority.

## 3. Identity and labels

The command already retains exact entity identity/content.

Presentation may snapshot the human name at command creation so later renaming does not make the old command misleading.

Undo/Redo continues to resolve by exact IDs/state.

Do not resolve command identity by current display name.

## 4. Menu labels

When available:

```text
Edit
Undo Move “Front Left”        Ctrl+Z
Redo Change screen height     Ctrl+Y
```

When no action exists, show generic disabled Undo/Redo.

Do not expose internal class names such as `TransformEntitiesCommand`.

## 5. Recent edit history

Provide an optional compact history surface, for example:

- Edit > Undo History…;
- small dropdown next to Undo;
- command palette entry.

Example:

```text
Current working edits

✓ Move Front Left
✓ Move Front Right
✓ Change screen height
→ current state
  Rotate projector        redo
```

The active index must be explicit.

This is not a permanent large dock.

## 6. Multi-step Undo

A history dropdown may later allow:

> Undo through “Change screen height”

by sequentially invoking the canonical Undo operation.

Before doing so:
- resolve/cancel active preview;
- preserve exact order;
- do not implement a second reverse-diff system.

MVP may keep the history read-only if multi-step UX is not yet justified.

## 7. Command granularity

Interactive drag should commit one semantic command at release/commit.

Avoid history like:

```text
Move FL +0.1 mm
Move FL +0.1 mm
Move FL +0.1 mm
...
```

Do not silently coalesce across unrelated subjects/actions.

## 8. Whole-document commands

`ReplaceDocumentCommand` is too generic for presentation.

Call sites should supply semantic intent where known:

- Edit room geometry;
- Apply selected SystemVariant;
- Restore design state;
- Change to

title: Physical attachment and assembly authority: support stands, mounts, racks and child-relative placement without mechanical-CAD scope
body:
## Summary

Deep Room-CAD/product-model review of HTDT `main@db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb` found that physical objects are still fundamentally independent world-pose entities.

This is sufficient for simple speakers/seats, but a real theater contains many **physical assemblies**:

- speaker on stand;
- speaker wall bracket / ceiling mount;
- projector attached to ceiling mount;
- display attached to wall bracket;
- screen attached to wall/frame;
- rack containing AVR/amplifiers/processors;
- seat with attached tactile transducer;
- equipment sitting on shelf;
- removable acoustic panel on support;
- masking panel attached to screen structure.

Today those relationships tend to be represented only by coincident geometry and human interpretation.

That creates a normal workflow problem:

> Moving the speaker stand does not inherently move the speaker.  
> Moving the equipment rack does not inherently preserve device slot positions.  
> A projector mount cannot be reasoned about separately from the projector it supports.

#641 already identifies “physical parent/support relation where canonical” as a likely stable Scene-core concept, but there is no dedicated authority/UX issue defining it.

## Goal

Add a bounded **Physical Attachment / Assembly Authority** for exact support/mount relationships and relative poses.

It should support common theater assemblies without turning Scene into a general mechanical assembly/CAD system.

Keep separate:

- purely visual/editor grouping;
- physical support/attachment;
- signal/electrical topology;
- semantic role binding.

## 1. Distinguish editor groups from physical assemblies

Two different features are needed.

### Editor group

Purpose:

- select several entities;
- hide/show together;
- move as a convenience where safe.

It is presentation/editing state unless explicitly committed as a structural relationship.

Examples:

- “front stage speakers”;
- “seat row 2” selection group.

### Physical attachment

Purpose:

> entity B is physically located relative to host/support entity A.

Examples:

- speaker mounted on stand;
- projector attached to ceiling mount;
- AVR installed in rack slot.

This affects physical geometry/installation semantics and belongs to Scene/project authority.

Do not make every Ctrl+G action a physical mount claim.

## 2. Suggested physical relation model

Conceptually:

```text
PhysicalAttachment
- attachment_id
- child_entity_id
- host_ref
- attachment_kind
- child_pose_in_host_frame
- anchor / interface info where known
- lifecycle/provenance
```

Host may be:

- another Scene entity;
- room surface;
- construction/support region;
- rack slot;
- installation datum/frame.

Attachment kinds may include:

- supported_by;
- mounted_to;
- installed_in;
- attached_to;
- suspended_from;
- user-defined bounded relation.

Do not use free-form strings as the only semantics.

## 3. Relative pose authority

When attached, store an exact **relative transform**.

Example:

```text
Stand S1 world pose
  ↓
Speaker FL relative pose to S1
  ↓
Speaker FL world pose derived
```

The relationship must define which pose is authoritative.

Avoid storing:

- independent mutable world pose;
- independent mutable relative pose;

as duplicate truths with no reconciliation rule.

A practical model may canonicalize:
- host world pose + child local pose;
- derive child world pose.

Historical migration may require adapters.

## 4. World-coordinate interoperability

Many existing consumers expect `SceneEntity.position/orientation`.

Do not force every solver/renderer to become hierarchy-aware immediately.

Provide deterministic world-pose resolution:

```text
resolve_world_pose(entity_id, SceneRevision)
```

with:

- cycle detection;
- exact transform composition;
- bounded depth;
- deterministic results.

Compiled/derived world poses are not a second editable truth.

## 5. Cycle prevention

Attachment graph must be acyclic.

Reject:

```text
A mounted to B
B mounted to A
```

title: Orientation UX: 本体と音響方向のYaw符号・Pitch/Rollの意味を、設置作業向けの共通表示に整理する
body:
## 要約 / 優先度

**推奨 P2 — 角度を正確に入力する通常操作で、隣接する欄が違う回転を意味する。**

#470で本体姿勢と音響照準を独立して編集できるようになった点は維持すべきです。一方、現行Inspectorは、二つの内部parameterizationをほぼそのまま同じYaw/Pitchという名前で表示しています。

- **本体Yawの正値**: +Y正面を−X側へ向ける。
- **音響Yawの正値**: +Yから+X側へ向ける。
- **本体Pitch**: 基準姿勢では正面軸周りのねじれで、正面の仰角は変わらない。
- **音響Pitch**: 仰角。
- 基準姿勢から本体正面を上下に傾けるのは、現行本体欄ではRoll。

内部数学の誤りではなく、設置角度を入力する製品の語彙・操作契約の不整合です。tooltipを読むと規約は分かりますが、同じ名前の数値をそのまま比較・転記できません。

## 実装根拠

- [room_workspace.py L782–805](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/room_workspace.py#L782-L805): 本体Yaw/Pitch/Rollのtooltipが上記規約を説明し、欄はそのままYaw/Pitch/Rollと表示。
- [L848–857](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/room_workspace.py#L848-L857): 音響Yawは+X側が正、音響Pitchは+Z側が正。
- [L1157–1177](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/room_workspace.py#L1157-L1177): 本体欄はEuler変換、音響欄は別のyaw/pitch変換を直接使用。
- [cad_scene.py L135–166](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/cad_scene.py#L135-L166): 本体はintrinsic Z-Y-X Euler。
- [cad_objects.py L31–69](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/cad_objects.py#L31-L69): aimは `atan2(x,y)` と仰角。
- [cad_objects.py L72–83](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/cad_objects.py#L72-L83): 「本体を方向に合わせる」は `body yaw=atan2(-x,y), body pitch=0, body roll=asin(z)` に変換。

## 確認用の通常シナリオ

水平のスピーカーで音響Yawを+30°にし、「本体を方向に合わせる」を実行します。

コード上は本体Yawが−30°、音響Yawが+30°になります。**同じ方向を向いた正しい結果が、数値上は符号不一致として現れます。**

さらに音響Pitchを+20°にすると、整列後の本体Euler欄は概ねYaw −30° / Pitch 0° / Roll +20°です。ユーザーが「Pitchも20°に揃える」と考えて本体Pitchを変更すると、狙った上下傾斜とは異なる回転を加えます。

これは静的な変換式から導いた確認シナリオであり、実機スクリーンショットによる再現報告ではありません。

## ユーザーへの影響

- Atmos/壁掛けスピーカーの上下角を入力する際に、ねじれと仰角を混同する。
- 同じ符号を入れて本体と音響照準を合わせたつもりでも、水平向きが離れる。
- 正しく整列済みでも、Inspectorが「異なる角度」に見える。
- Optimizeのaim/body値や設置資料を転記する際、変換規約の知識が必要になる。

本体と音響照準が独立してよいことと、同じ表示名が違う意味でよいことは別問題です。

## 改善案

### 1. 通常表示を作業上の角度へ

本体正面と音響照準について、共通の基準で「水平向き」「仰角」を表示します。本体には独立して「正面軸周りのねじれ」を表示できます。

```
本体の向き                 音響方向
水平向き  右へ30°          水平向き  右へ30°
仰角      上へ20°          仰角      上へ20°
ねじれ    0°

正面と音響方向: 一致
[本体を音響方向へ合わせる]
```

正方向・基準方向を画面内の簡潔な表示または小さな方向図で示し、tooltipだけに依存しない。日本語の「右/左」は部屋座標・観察者視点のどちらかを明示して決めます。

### 2. 内部Eulerと保存データは保持

既存quaternion、O80/O90のパラメーター、保存済みSceneRevisionを改変しない。通常入力からquaternionへの明示的な変換adapterを用意し、必要なら「詳細: Z-Y-X Euler」を残します。

単純にPitchとRollの見出しを入れ替えるだけでは複合回転・ねじれを正しく扱えません。body-forwardベクトルとup/twistの関係から定義し、既存任意姿勢の表示・編集round-tripを設計してください。

### 3. 比較は角度の意味を揃える

本体正面とaimの差を示す場合は、別規約の数値の差ではなく、world-spaceの向きから導く。音響aim不明時は不明と表示し、本体から勝手に推定しない。

### 4. 一つの表示契約を再利用

Room、Optimize候補、robustness設定、設置図/レポートで同じ意味の角度を同じラベル・符号で提示します。Captureの将来の3D aim入力とも規約を照合しますが、各製品の内部座標系を統合する必要はありません。

## 受け入れ条件

- [ ] 本体をaimへ整列した状態では、通常表示の水平向き・仰角が意味上一致する。
- [ ] 通常表示の仰角を変更すると本体正面が上下に動き、ねじれを変更すると仰角を意図せず変更しない。
- [ ] 本体編集はaimを変更せず、aim編集は本体を変更しない。
- [ ] 既存の任意quaternionを表示しただけで姿勢・精度・SceneRevisionが変わらない。
- [ ] ±30°の水平、±20°の仰角、複合姿勢、ねじれ、前後左右の代表方向を確認する。
- [ ] 垂直方向など水平向きが定義できない状態を、確定した0°として誤解させない。
- [ ] Undo/Redo、精密数値入力、候補適用後の再表示に同じ変換契約を使う。
- [ ] 既存のEuler/O80/O90 persisted parameter semanticsを無言で変更しない。
- [ ] 内部規約を必要とする利用者には、詳細画面で正確なEuler値を確認できる。

## 関連 / レビュー範囲

- #470: 編集機能の実装は完了。本件はその後に露出した表示規約の不整合。
- #583: Inspectorの共通部品・説明・入力状態。
- #644: 設置図に出す角度の意味。
- HTDT-Capture #228: full 3D aim。

GitHub main `db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb` の静的レビュー。既存open/closed issueを検索し、この符号・意味の不一致を直接扱うissueは確認できませんでした。実機確認・コード変更は未実施。

title: Measurement import: 取得時のSceneRevisionを明示選択し、後日取り込む実測を最新配置へ自動結合しない
body:
## 要約 / 優先度

**推奨 P1 — 通常の実測取り込みで、証拠が何の配置を表すかを誤らせる製品仕様の問題。**

現在のMeasurementsは、REWの測定を読み込む時点のlatest SceneRevisionを自動的に選びます。実際の取得時に使った過去の配置を選択する欄はありません。

「測定データを不変のSceneRevisionに結合する」実装自体はありますが、**取得時の配置と取り込み時の最新配置が同じであるという、確認されていない前提**が残っています。稀な競合や破損の話ではなく、測定をまとめて後から取り込む通常の使い方に関わります。

## 現行mainで確認した根拠

1. [measurement_workflow.py L234–274](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/measurement_workflow.py#L234-L274): `stage_rew_text()` と `stage_rew_snapshot()` はどちらも `latest_revision()` を呼び、pendingにrevision ID/hashを設定します。取得時のrevisionを渡す引数がありません。
2. [L290–323](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/measurement_workflow.py#L290-L323): 割り当て可能な測定点・スピーカーはこのpending revisionから列挙されます。
3. [L325–366](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/measurement_workflow.py#L325-L366): 保存時にもlatestとpendingの一致を要求し、不一致なら「REWを読み込み直して」と案内します。pendingの元revisionが正常に存在しても、履歴への保存を選ぶことはできません。
4. [measurement_page_workspace.py L482–555](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/src/htdt/measurement_page_workspace.py#L482-L555): 割り当て画面には測定位置・証拠種別・入力役割・放射範囲・ルーティング根拠・音源がありますが、取得時の配置の選択・確認がありません。
5. [既存テスト L96–119](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb/backend/tests/test_measurement_workflow_ux130.py#L96-L119) は、取り込み中に保存済み配置が変わると拒否する現在の契約を明示的に固定しています。これは削除すべき安全策ではなく、明示的な履歴取り込みを別途設計すべきことを示します。

## 通常の利用シナリオ

### A: 配置A/Bの測定を後でまとめて取り込む

1. 配置R10でFL/FR/CをREW測定する。
2. スピーカー・座席を動かし、HTDTでR11を保存する。
3. R10で取得したREWファイルを取り込む。
4. 現行実装はR11の測定点・音源・位置に結合する経路を提示する。

raw FRの値が正しくても、保存された空間的意味付けが取得時と一致する保証がありません。結果として、配置改善の比較、予測との誤差解釈、測定計画への割り当てを誤る可能性があります。下流の品質gateがすべて通る、とまでは主張しません。

### B: 取り込み途中に新しい配置を保存する

R10をstageした後でRoomへ移りR11を保存すると、R10への明示的な確定操作がなく、読み直しを要求されます。案内に従うと同じ測定bytesがR11へstageされます。「読み直し」は取得時の配置を確認する代わりになりません。

## 改善する製品契約

### 1. 取得時の配置と取り込み時の配置を分離

割り当て前に次を提示してください。

```
この測定を取得したときの配置
[現在の保存済み配置 R11] [履歴から選ぶ…] [まだ分からない]

選択: 測定前チェックポイント R10
現在の配置との差: FL移動 / 測定点移動
```

- 現在の配置は提案として使えますが、取得時の状態であることをユーザーが確認できるようにする。
- 履歴のIDだけでなく名前・保存日時・簡潔な差分・空間previewを使う。
- filename、REW UUID、取得日時だけでrevisionを断定しない。
- 過去revisionを選んでもプロジェクトのcurrent headは変更しない。

### 2. revision選択を割り当ての基準にする

選択したexact revision内の測定点、音源、位置から割り当てを生成します。途中でrevisionを変えた場合は、以前のentity IDが一致していても内容の再確認を要求し、存在しない測定点への自動置換をしないでください。

### 3. 最新配置が変化した場合

黙って再結合しない既存保護を維持しつつ、次を分けます。

- 選択済みR10への履歴取り込みを続ける。
- 別のrevisionを選び、割り当てを再確認する。
- キャンセルしてpendingを保持する。

「読み込み直し」だけを解決手段にしない。

### 4. 取得時の配置が不明な実測

raw evidenceを保留として保持できるようにします。既存のcanonical measurementがexact SceneRevision必須なら、そのモデルを弱めず、import staging側で未解決として扱う。最新配置を捏造して正規measurementへ昇格させない。

### 5. 画面と履歴の一貫性

確定前サマリーに取得時の配置・測定点・音源を表示し、履歴への取り込みであることを明記します。取り込み日時と取得日時を区別し、後から取り込んだデータを事前登録済みcampaignに自動的に適合させないでください。

## 既存issueとの責務分担

- #487: 保存済みmeasurementの歴史的な空間表示。本件は**保存前のrevision選択**。
- #485: 履歴の選択・previewを再利用する。履歴復元は要求しない。
- #509: 誤割当の事後訂正。本件は入口で誤割当を予防。
- #471: マイク・AVRなどの取得条件。本件は空間revision。
- #446 / #529: batch/campaignも各itemの取得時revisionを明示的に引き継ぐ。
- #626: latest headの定義が修正されても、本件の「latest＝取得時」の前提は残る。

## 受け入れ条件

- [ ] currentがR11でも、R10で取得したREW text/API snapshotをR10へ明示的に取り込める。
- [ ] 保存結果のrevision ID/hash、測定点座標、音源は選択したR10に一致する。
- [ ] 操作によってcurrent head R11が変わらない。
- [ ] R10 stage後にR11が保存されても、無言で再結合せず、履歴として続行/再割り当て/保留を選べる。
- [ ] revision選択変更後に無効になった割り当ては未確認になる。
- [ ] 取得時配置が不明なraw evidenceを保留でき、通常のmeasured evidenceとして誤昇格させない。
- [ ] batchで異なる取得時revisionを扱え、一括操作が無言で上書きしない。
- [ ] 保存前後の表示で「現在の配置」と「この測定の配置」が区別できる。
- [ ] 既存のstale検出、不変証拠、campaign事前登録の制約を維持する。

## レビュー記録

- GitHub main: `db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb`
- GitHub上の実装・既存テスト・open/closed issuesを静的確認。実機再現・ローカル変更・テスト実行は行っていません。
- 提案はUI/取り込み契約の改善であり、ソルバーや既存証拠の書き換えを要求しません。

title: Connected-space promotion contract: bridge Capture regions/portals into HTDT physical spaces without flattening to one RoomPrism
body:
## Summary

Cross-repository connected-space review found a major product-model gap between what HTDT-Capture can now preserve and what HTDT's primary Scene model can currently represent.

HTDT-Capture #222 implements a persisted ConnectedSpaceDocument containing:

- one Capture revision;
- one shared coordinate space;
- multiple CaptureRegionSegment records;
- explicit CaptureRegionPortal edges.

Region kinds include room, open-plan area, hallway, stairwell, alcove and other. Portal kinds include doorway, open passage, stair opening and other.

The current Capture invariants are strong:

- all connected segments share one exact coordinate authority;
- portal endpoints are exact region IDs;
- independent coordinate spaces cannot be silently linked;
- evidence refs are preserved.

#222 explicitly expects downstream HTDT to promote connected regions/portals without heuristic filename or label matching.

HTDT's physical Scene model, however, is still centered on one SceneDocument.room: RoomPrism, while #101/R110 uses or plans AcousticRegion / Portal concepts at solver level.

There is no explicit product contract for the middle step:

Capture connected-space evidence
→ HTDT physical/project region interpretation
→ solver AcousticRegion / Portal authority

Without it, realistic open-plan/adjacent-space captures risk being flattened, discarded or over-promoted.

## Why this matters

Common theater environments include:

- theater opening to a hallway;
- living room connected to kitchen/dining;
- stairwell adjacent to listening area;
- alcove or vestibule;
- double-height space;
- equipment closet;
- adjacent room relevant to sound isolation.

Bad fallback options are not acceptable:

### Flatten everything into one polygon room

This loses region identity, portal relationships, room-specific state/material semantics and future isolation reasoning.

### Import only the main room

This silently discards captured evidence.

### Turn Capture segment labels directly into AcousticRegion

This promotes acquisition workflow segmentation into solver-ready semantic truth.

### Split connected regions into unrelated projects

This destroys the exact shared coordinate and portal relationships.

## Goal

Define a Connected Physical Space / Region Promotion Contract between Capture connected-space evidence and HTDT Scene/acoustic-region authority.

Preserve the following stages explicitly:

1. Capture acquisition region;
2. HTDT physical-space interpretation;
3. acoustic solver region/portal interpretation.

No layer should silently stand in for all three.

## 1. Distinguish three region concepts

### CaptureRegionSegment

Acquisition/workflow evidence from HTDT-Capture.

Meaning:

The operator treated this evidence subset as one connected scan region.

It does not automatically prove room-boundary topology, architectural room identity or a closed acoustic volume.

### PhysicalSpaceRegion

HTDT project-level spatial interpretation.

Meaning:

These surfaces/volumes belong to one physically meaningful area in the project.

Examples:
- theater;
- hallway;
- open-plan kitchen;
- stairwell.

This should own physical region identity and geometry relationships.

### AcousticRegion

#101/R110 solver-facing acoustic volume.

Meaning:

A solver region with sufficiently defined geometry/boundary/portal semantics for a selected model.

A PhysicalSpaceRegion may map 1:1 to one AcousticRegion, be merged, be split, or remain unsupported/uncompiled.

Do not bind these concepts by human name alone.

## 2. Evolve Scene without turning HTDT into BIM

Current SceneDocument has one primary room.

Define an explicit migration direction rather than adding unrelated secondary-room sidecars.

A bounded first design could keep legacy room compatibility while adding an optional connected-space model containing:

- stable physical region IDs;
- exact region geometry refs;
- portal/opening refs;
- one shared project coordinate frame;
- primary-theater role.

Collision geometry refinement: rich mesh bodies still use bounding-envelope clearance despite exact visual geometry
body:
## Summary

Deep geometry/constraint review of HTDT `main@db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb` found that #464 is only partially realized for **collision / clearance authority**.

#464 was closed with an acceptance criterion:

> Collision/clearance can consume explicit collision geometry where available and retain bounded-envelope fallback where not.

The current implementation does consume exact authored shape for a bounded subset:

- upright `cylinder`;
- upright `extruded_polygon`.

But `entity_exact_body_footprint()` explicitly returns `None` for:

- `mesh_asset`;
- tilted/pitched/rolled extrusion bodies;
- box/no refined body.

Those cases fall back to the convex hull of the oriented `size_m` envelope.

Therefore the current behavior is:

```text
Viewport
  mesh_asset -> exact imported mesh is visible

Collision / wall clearance / region / pair envelope
  mesh_asset -> bounding size_m box projection
```

The same visually detailed entity can therefore appear to fit while placement constraints reject it because its bounding box overlaps a walkway/wall — or conversely a poor envelope can hide useful exact clearance geometry.

This is not a rare numerical edge case.

Imported furniture, recliners, curved seats, equipment racks, projector bodies and irregular loudspeaker cabinets are precisely the object classes #464 introduced rich body geometry for.

## Current implementation evidence

### Rendering

`room_viewport._entity_mesh()` renders:

- cylinder;
- extruded polygon;
- imported mesh asset;

and separately displays the `size_m` envelope wireframe.

### Collision/clearance

`cad_orientation_constraints.entity_exact_body_footprint()` only recognizes:

```python
body.kind in ('cylinder', 'extruded_polygon')
and local Z remains world-up
```

The docstring explicitly says:

> Returns None for entities without exact extrusion geometry (box, mesh_asset, missing size) and for tilted bodies...

`entity_collision_geometry_authority()` therefore reports:

- `exact_body_geometry`; or
- `bounding_envelope`.

`cad_constraints._entity_profile()` consumes `entity_horizontal_footprint()`, so allowed/exclusion/wall-clearance/pair-distance constraints inherit the fallback.

## Why this matters

### Example 1 — sofa

Imported L-shaped sofa mesh:

- bounding envelope: 2.8 × 1.8 m;
- actual footprint has a large empty corner.

A walkway in that empty corner is rejected because the broad box overlaps it.

### Example 2 — projector

Projector body/lens geometry may occupy a smaller irregular footprint than its shipping/catalog envelope.

A ceiling-service clearance check can be unnecessarily conservative.

### Example 3 — reclined/tilted body

A body with pitch/roll can render at its actual pose but collision uses a conservative oriented box hull.

That is safe but can materially shrink feasible design space.

### Example 4 — imported rack/furniture

The user sees exact mesh geometry and may reasonably expect visible clearance to correspond to the constraint result.

Without an explicit authority indicator, the mismatch is confusing.

## Goal

Introduce a clear, bounded **collision geometry authority** for rich Scene bodies.

Support increasingly precise collision/clearance where mathematically and operationally justified, while preserving conservative fallback.

Do not require full triangle-mesh collision for every query.

## 1. Freeze geometry roles

Keep these distinct:

```text
display geometry
broad-phase envelope
horizontal clearance footprint
3D collision geometry
operational/swept clearance      #655? actually #651
acoustic geometry
```

A Scene body may provide different precision for each.

Do not use one ambiguous term “mesh”.

## 2. Explicit collision geometry mode

Conceptually add/read a derived contract:

```text
EntityCollisionGeometry
- source body authority
- broad_phase
- horizontal footprint mode
- 3D collision mode
- approximation class
- algorithm/version
```

Possible modes:

- exact parametric;
- exact polygon extr

title: Product Domain Boundary Charter: keep HTDT a theater Digital Twin while bounding BIM, calibration, electrical, lighting and procurement scope
Design Decision Record: explicitly record which alternative was adopted, why, and for what lifecycle scope
body:
## Summary

Deep design-lifecycle review of HTDT `main@db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb` found that the product increasingly preserves **the alternatives and the evidence**, but not yet a first-class record of **the user's actual design decision**.

Existing/planned authorities cover adjacent concerns well:

- #447 DesignComparisonSet — freeze named alternatives for comparison;
- #594 AnalysisStudy — save reproducible analysis views and engineering notes;
- #619 ProjectDesignCheckpoint — freeze a broad design-state manifest;
- SystemVariant — represent proposed system changes;
- explicit SystemVariant apply — create new SceneRevision;
- #615 Project lifecycle timeline — show significant events;
- #520 commissioning — compare intended/as-built/measured state.

What remains missing is the bounded transition:

> I reviewed alternatives A/B/C and explicitly chose B for this design stage because of these stated tradeoffs/constraints.

Applying a Scene/SystemVariant is an action.

A comparison set is a set of options.

An AnalysisStudy is analysis context.

A checkpoint is a state snapshot.

None necessarily means:

> this is the chosen alternative, and here is the rationale/evidence context for that choice.

## Why this matters

A mature theater project may contain many plausible alternatives:

- seat forward vs back;
- toe-in alternatives;
- 3.0.2 vs 5.0.2;
- treatment A vs B;
- speaker replacement choices;
- projector/image profiles;
- calibration target variants;
- installation compromises.

Months later the user needs to answer:

- Why did I choose this?
- Which alternatives were considered?
- Was the choice based on prediction, measured evidence, installation limits, cost, or preference?
- Was it only a design preference, or did it represent physical installation?
- Has later evidence invalidated the rationale?
- Did I explicitly accept an unresolved assumption?

Without a typed decision record, that knowledge is spread among notes, current state, comparison views and memory.

## Goal

Add an immutable **DesignDecisionRecord** that references existing exact authorities.

It should record:

> selected alternative + considered alternatives + bounded rationale + decision scope

without becoming an automatic recommendation engine.

HTDT must continue to present evidence/tradeoffs neutrally; the human makes the decision.

## 1. Decision is distinct from comparison

### DesignComparisonSet #447
> What alternatives are being compared?

### AnalysisStudy #594
> What analysis view/notes were used?

### DesignDecisionRecord
> Which alternative did the user explicitly select for a stated purpose?

Do not add a hidden “winner” to `DesignComparisonSet`.

Selection is a separate explicit user action.

## 2. Suggested authority

Conceptually:

```text
DesignDecisionRecord
- decision_id
- project_id
- created_at
- title
- decision_scope
- selected_ref
- considered_refs[]
- comparison_set_ref?
- analysis_study_refs[]
- design_checkpoint_ref?
- stated_rationale[]
- accepted_tradeoffs[]
- accepted_assumption_refs[]
- lifecycle_intent
- supersedes?
- author/origin
- schema_version / semantic hash
```

This is mostly a manifest of exact refs + human rationale.

Do not copy scientific result arrays into it.

## 3. Decision scope

A decision must say what it means.

Suggested scopes:

- exploratory preference;
- selected design direction;
- ready for installation planning;
- installation concession;
- calibration/settings choice;
- equipment substitution choice;
- commissioning acceptance/waiver;
- user-defined bounded scope.

Do not make “selected design direction” imply physically installed.

## 4. Lifecycle intent

Keep these distinct:

```text
choose for further design
choose to apply to project design
choose for installation
accept as-built deviation
accept commissioning limitation
```

Actual state changes still happen through their canonical owner:

- SceneRevision apply;
- SystemVariant apply;
- installed/as-built authority;
- calibr

title: Mesh body asset boundary: stop embedding full triangle geometry in every immutable SceneRevision
body:
## Summary

Deep implementation/authority-storage review of HTDT `main@db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb` after #464 found an important scaling mismatch in the new mesh-backed physical body model.

#464 correctly introduced a content-addressed blob store and gives imported mesh bodies exact provenance through:

```text
asset_sha256
source_name
asset_format
original_size_bytes
```

However, `BodyMeshAsset` also stores the complete normalized geometry inline inside each `SceneEntity`:

```python
vertices: tuple[BodyMeshVertex, ...]
triangles: tuple[BodyMeshTriangle, ...]
```

`SceneRepository` then serializes the full `SceneDocument` to `scene_revisions.payload_json` for **every immutable SceneRevision**.

Therefore an unchanged imported object mesh is duplicated into every later SceneRevision JSON whenever the user moves another speaker, edits a seat, saves a dimension change, etc.

The original asset bytes are simultaneously retained in the content-addressed blob store.

This makes the feature described as “asset-backed mesh” effectively:

```text
original blob
+
full normalized mesh embedded in every SceneRevision
```

For non-trivial meshes this can make ordinary project history, recovery snapshots, hashing, save/open, backup and diff behavior scale with:

```text
mesh size × number of SceneRevisions
```

rather than with actual changed project state.

## Why this is a product-level issue

This is not mainly about saving a few megabytes.

HTDT's core product contract is immutable revision history.

If richer furniture/equipment meshes are encouraged, a static visual asset should not make every minor edit create another large geometry copy.

Expected user workflow:

1. import one sofa/chair/rack mesh;
2. keep editing speaker/seat/layout dozens or hundreds of times;
3. retain SceneRevision history;
4. create backups/project bundles;
5. browse history and compare revisions.

The data architecture should make this workflow cheap enough that users do not need to avoid rich body geometry.

## Goal

Make mesh-backed SceneEntity bodies **truly asset-backed**.

Persist normalized geometry once as immutable content-addressed project asset authority and let SceneRevision carry a compact exact reference.

Preserve:

- deterministic geometry;
- exact content identity;
- original-source provenance;
- local transform;
- reopenability;
- immutable revision semantics.

Do not weaken #464's exact-geometry contract.

## 1. Separate source asset from normalized body geometry

There are conceptually two assets.

### Original source asset

Examples:

- OBJ;
- GLB;
- imported `.htdt_meshbin_v1`.

Authority:

- original bytes;
- source filename;
- format;
- SHA-256;
- import provenance.

### Normalized body geometry asset

HTDT's deterministic local-coordinate geometry used for display/collision:

- vertices;
- triangles;
- normalization/schema version;
- canonical byte representation;
- SHA-256.

The normalized asset may be derived from the source.

Do not require reparsing arbitrary source files every time a SceneRevision opens.

## 2. Compact Scene reference

Replace or evolve inline `BodyMeshAsset` toward something conceptually like:

```text
BodyMeshReference
- geometry_asset_sha256
- geometry_format = htdt_meshbin_v1
- source_asset_sha256
- source_name
- source_format
- original_size_bytes
- local_offset
- uniform_scale
- optional compact bounds/summary
```

Exact names are flexible.

The Scene content hash remains exact because it includes the normalized geometry digest.

Changing mesh content changes the digest and therefore changes Scene content identity.

## 3. Canonical normalized mesh format

Persist one deterministic body-mesh representation.

Requirements:

- versioned magic/schema;
- finite coordinates;
- indexed triangles;
- deterministic endianness/order;
- bounded counts/sizes;
- canonical serialization;
- exact hash.

Reuse `htdt_meshbin_v1` if its contract is suitable.

title: Installation feasibility authority: mounting substrate, framing/cavity, cutout and service constraints without becoming BIM
Operational geometry and swept-clearance authority for doors, recliners, service access and movable equipment
body:
## Summary

Deep CAD/product-boundary review of HTDT `main@db35b4fcaa3776930274077b6432cdfb066458bb` found a practical gap between the increasingly accurate **static** geometry model and real home-theater installation/use constraints.

Recent body-geometry work (#464) can represent:

- box;
- cylinder;
- extruded polygon;
- imported mesh body;

and use that geometry for display/collision.

Placement constraints can represent:

- allowed regions;
- exclusion/walkway regions;
- wall clearance;
- pair distance;
- axis/movement/linked relationships in the optimization path.

What is still missing is the geometry of an object **while it operates or is accessed**.

Examples:

- a door leaf can fit at the closed pose but collide with a speaker when opened;
- a recliner fits upright but blocks a walkway/surround when reclined;
- a cabinet/rack front or rear door needs an opening/service sweep;
- an AVR/amplifier can fit on a shelf but its rear connectors need service space;
- a projector mount may need an adjustment/service zone;
- an equipment rack needs front/rear maintenance approach space;
- a movable acoustic panel can have deployed/stowed envelopes.

These are not rare edge cases. They determine whether a layout is physically usable.

## Goal

Add a bounded **Operational Geometry / Swept Clearance** authority that is separate from the static physical body.

It should answer:

> Given this explicit operating state/action, what space must remain clear?

Do not turn HTDT into a general rigid-body/robotics simulator.

## 1. Keep static body truth separate

Current `SceneEntity.body_geometry` remains the actual authored body shape at a specific Scene pose.

Do not redefine body geometry as “maximum possible footprint”.

Add a separate concept, for example:

```text
OperationalEnvelopeDefinition
- exact entity / equipment binding
- operation kind
- reference body/local frame
- state/parameter domain
- swept geometry or clearance geometry
- source/provenance
- confidence/applicability
```

A large conservative operational envelope must never be mistaken for the actual cabinet size.

## 2. Initial operation classes

Start with bounded high-value patterns.

### Door / hinged leaf

Represent:

- hinge axis/side;
- leaf dimensions;
- closed/open angle range;
- optional handle clearance margin.

Evaluate a swept arc/prism.

Do not infer hinge side from RoomPlan wall ordering unless explicitly supported.

### Recliner / articulating seat

MVP may use explicit authored state envelopes:

- upright body;
- reclined body;
- transition/swept envelope where known.

Do not require a detailed mechanism model.

If only manufacturer “required wall clearance” exists, retain that as a documented clearance requirement rather than inventing kinematics.

### Sliding/drawer/pull-out service

Represent a translation direction + required extension envelope.

Examples:

- equipment drawer;
- pull-out rack;
- cabinet door;
- removable projector/filter service access.

### Service approach zone

Deep source/headroom review of HTDT `main@6ad227fafc88c6f19e0bdda927114326e2d5a081` found that EquipmentDefinition can represent a scalar declared:
- continuous SPL;
- peak SPL;
- duration;
- valid frequency domain;

and #477/#544 can model amplifier/electrical limits.

What is missing is an authority for the **quality-limited acoustic output behavior** of a loudspeaker/subwoofer as level increases.

Repository/issue search found no model for:
- output compression vs level/frequency;
- distortion-limited max usable SPL;
- THD/harmonic distortion measurements;
- excursion-limited band/capability;
- limiter onset/behavior;
- level-dependent source response.

This matters because:

> a speaker can be electrically driveable to a requested level while already exhibiting substantial compression/distortion, especially at low frequency.

A single manufacturer `peak SPL` number does not establish the same engineering claim as a measured frequency-dependent usable-output profile.

## Goal

Add a bounded **Nonlinear / Usable Output Capability** authority for speakers and subwoofers.

Initial scope is evidence storage, capability gating and headroom comparison.

Do not implement a full nonlinear transducer/time-domain room solver.

## 1. Separate declared level from usable-output evidence

Keep existing `SplCapability` valid for declared scalar capability.

Add a separate authority that can answer:

> At this frequency/band and reference condition, what output level was observed before a stated compression/distortion/limiter criterion was reached?

Do not reinterpret existing continuous/peak SPL as distortion-qualified unless its source evidence explicitly says so.

## 2. Capability tiers

Possible tiers:
- UNKNOWN;
- scalar declared max SPL;
- frequency-dependent max-output curve with method;
- compression-vs-level data;
- THD/harmonic-vs-level data;
- combined measured usable-output profile;
- excursion/model-limited analytic profile.

Each tier opens only justified calculations.

## 3. Canonical evidence authority

Conceptually:

```text
SourceUsableOutputProfile
- profile_id / version / semantic hash
- exact EquipmentDefinition ref
- mounting/reference condition
- measurement distance/environment
- excitation/test method
- frequency/band samples
- output level
- compression metric where available
- distortion metric where available
- limiter/thermal state where known
- valid level/frequency domain
- provenance/raw asset/parser
- uncertainty
```

Do not force every profile to contain every nonlinear metric.

## 4. Compression

Represent output compression relative to an explicit low/reference-level response.

Example semantics:

```text
frequency
input/reference level
expected linear increase
observed output
compression dB
```

Do not compute compression against an arbitrary unrelated sensitivity specification.

The baseline/reference measurement must be explicit.

## 5. Distortion

Support exact measured distortion quantities where evidence exists.

At minimum distinguish:
- THD;
- individual harmonic orders where available;
- noise/distortion aggregate if that is what the source reports;
- metric unavailable.

Store method/bandwidth/reference semantics.

Do not label all nonlinear residuals `THD`.

## 6. Distortion threshold

A `usable output` evaluation may bind a project/user/reference criterion such as:

```text
compression <= X dB
THD <= Y %
```

but threshold is policy, not intrinsic truth.

Keep:
- measured profile;
- selected criterion;
- derived usable limit

as separate authorities/results.

Do not hard-code one universal acceptable THD value.

## 7. Frequency dependence

Usable output must be frequency/band aware.

Typical low-frequency capability can vary materially across:
- tuning region;
- crossover region;
- upper bass/midrange.

Do not convert one broadband/1 kHz max-SPL number into a full-band ceiling.

## 8. Subwoofer-specific evidence

Subwoofers may have dedicated burst/output test data.

## Summary

Deep playback-chain review of HTDT `main@6ad227fafc88c6f19e0bdda927114326e2d5a081` found that O100D/#477/#544 model the **power-amplifier output -> speaker electrical/acoustic headroom** side well, but the upstream line-level gain structure is not represented as a first-class authority.

Current `AmplifierOutputCapability` includes:
- amplifier gain;
- a reference input value;
- clipping reference definition;
- output/load capability.

That is useful for one amplifier stage, but there is no canonical chain for:

```text
digital source
-> AVR/processor DSP
-> DAC / pre-out
-> optional external DSP
-> optional level converter
-> power-amplifier input
-> power-amplifier output
-> speaker
```

Repository/issue search found no authority for:
- pre-out maximum/nominal voltage;
- analog input maximum level;
- line-stage gain/attenuation;
- balanced/unbalanced level semantics;
- DSP input/output clip ceiling;
- channel trim + master-volume operating point;
- PEQ/crossover gain contribution to digital headroom;
- summing headroom;
- end-to-end gain-structure evaluation.

This creates an important ordinary-system gap:

> HTDT can report enough amplifier/speaker output capability while the actual configured chain clips at the AVR pre-out, external DSP input/output, or digital processing stage first.

## Goal

Add a bounded **Line-Level Gain Structure / Signal Headroom** authority and evaluator that composes with #477 rather than replacing it.

HTDT should answer:
- which stage limits first;
- how much margin remains at each stage;
- whether the power amp can be driven to required output;
- whether trims/EQ/summing consume digital or analog headroom;
- which parts remain UNKNOWN.

Do not turn HTDT into a full SPICE/audio-circuit simulator.

## 1. Keep distinct headroom domains

Separate at least:

### Digital processing headroom
> Margin below the digital processing/representation clip point under an exact processing condition.

### Analog line-level headroom
> Margin below an analog output/input stage's evidenced maximum level.

### Power-amplifier output headroom
> Existing #477/#544 voltage/current/power capability into the speaker load.

### Acoustic headroom
> Resulting source/SPL capability.

Do not collapse all into one generic `headroom dB` without identifying the domain and limiting stage.

## 2. Typed line-level stage capability

Introduce a reusable immutable authority, conceptually:

```text
LineLevelStageCapability
- stage/device/port identity
- input level domain
- output level domain
- nominal/reference level
- maximum evidenced input level
- maximum evidenced output level
- gain/attenuation range
- fixed gain where applicable
- load/source conditions where relevant
- balanced/unbalanced topology metadata where evidenced
- valid frequency/domain condition
- provenance
- uncertainty
```

Not every field is required for every stage.

UNKNOWN remains valid.

Use canonical physical quantities internally.

Prefer:
- V RMS for analog voltage;
- dBFS for digital signal level relative to a defined full-scale convention;
- explicit dBu/dBV only as input/display units converted to physical/reference quantities.

Do not compare `0 dBFS`, `0 dBu` and `0 dBV` as if they share one zero point.

Conversion must retain the originating reference convention.

Capability belongs to an exact port/path where necessary.

Examples:
- AVR RCA pre-out;
- AVR XLR pre-out;
- DSP analog input 1;
- DSP analog output 1;
- amplifier balanced input;
- amplifier unbalanced input.

Do not assume every connector on one device has the same maximum level.

Compose with InstalledEquipmentInstance #569 and signal path #570.

A downstream stage may clip before the upstream source reaches its own maximum.

Example:

```text
processor pre-out max       4.0 V RMS
DSP analog input max        2.0 V RMS
```

## Summary

Deep installation/commissioning review of HTDT `main@6ad227fafc88c6f19e0bdda927114326e2d5a081` found that the product can plan cable routes and logical routing, but lacks a first-class **speaker wiring / channel electrical commissioning** workflow.

Existing issues cover adjacent concerns:
- #538 CableRun: planned physical cable routing/endpoints;
- #473 RoutingProfile: output/channel -> observed physical speaker mapping;
- #505 topology: logical role -> physical source;
- #520 CommissioningPlan/Run: general verification framework;
- MeasurementQuality: acoustic polarity capability.

What is not explicitly modeled is the ordinary installation checklist answering:
- Is this cable connected end-to-end?
- Does AVR/amp output X reach the intended physical speaker?
- Is terminal polarity consistent?
- Does the acoustic response indicate a polarity inversion?
- Is the measured load broadly compatible with the expected speaker/wiring?
- If something is wrong, is the cause known or merely observed?

These are common commissioning tasks, not rare failures.

## Goal

Add a typed **Speaker/Channel Wiring Verification** check family under #520.

Keep electrical continuity, logical routing, acoustic polarity and impedance/load observations as separate evidence types.

Do not infer hidden wire topology or automatically diagnose a cause from one failed check.

## 1. Separate the checks

### Logical channel routing
> Output/channel X caused physical source Y to radiate.

Canonical authority: #473 RoutingProfile.

### Cable continuity
> A visible/testable electrical path exists between selected endpoints.

### Terminal polarity
> The conductor/terminal relationship is consistent with the declared +/− convention.

### Acoustic polarity
> The observed acoustic response has the expected polarity under a defined measurement method.

### Load/impedance sanity
> An electrical measurement at a defined test point is compatible/incompatible/unknown relative to explicit equipment/wiring expectations.

None of these alone proves all the others.

## 2. Verification check authority

Add typed commissioning checks, conceptually:

```text
WiringVerificationCheck
- check_id
- check_kind
- expected endpoint/path/source refs
- method/instrument
- observed result
- evidence refs
- timestamp
- operator
- result: PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN / NOT_APPLICABLE
- reason
```

Checks live inside or are referenced by exact CommissioningRun #520.

## 3. Endpoint identity

Reuse exact infrastructure identities from #538.

Possible endpoints:
- amplifier/AVR output channel;
- rack terminal/patch panel;
- wall plate;
- speaker terminal;
- tactile amplifier/actuator where #638 applies.

Do not identify a wire only as free text `rear left cable` when exact endpoints exist.

## 4. Cable continuity

Support manual/instrument evidence such as:
- continuity confirmed;
- open circuit observed;
- short observed;
- unknown/not tested.

Bind:
- exact endpoints;
- instrument profile where used;
- test condition;
- evidence/note.

Do not interpret continuity PASS as correct channel routing or correct polarity.

## 5. Terminal polarity

Represent the expected conductor convention explicitly.

Example:

```text
Amp channel FL +
-> cable conductor red
-> speaker FL +
```

Verification may be:
- visually confirmed;
- continuity-probed;
- tone/polarity tester;
- unknown.

Do not silently assume cable color means electrical polarity.

## 6. Acoustic polarity

MeasurementQuality already has polarity evidence/capability.

Commissioning should reference exact acoustic measurement evidence when using it.

Important distinction:
> acoustic inversion observed

does not prove:
> speaker wire terminals are reversed.

Possible causes include:
- wiring inversion;
- DSP/channel polarity setting;
- active speaker internal behavior;
- measurement/reference method;
- routing mistake.

Report the observation first; diagnosis requires additional evidence.

```text
common_timing requires:

- timing reference
```

#471 plans physical AcquisitionContext and notes USB microphone / HDMI playback conditions matter for timing capability.

But there is still no canonical object answering:

> What exact timing reference made these measurements comparable in absolute/inter-channel time, how was it established, and which measurements share it?

## Why this is a product-level gap

Common timing is needed for normal advanced home-theater workflows:
- speaker/sub arrival alignment;
- impulse arrival-time comparison;
- phase alignment across separately acquired channels;
- excess delay / time-of-flight interpretation;
- measured-vs-predicted timing validation;
- calibration verification;

- USB microphone clock + HDMI output clock;
- REW acoustic timing reference;
- loopback/reference channel;

Introduce an immutable/versioned **MeasurementTimingReference / TimingSession** authority and native workflow.

## Summary

Deep schema/product-boundary review of HTDT `main@6ad227fafc88c6f19e0bdda927114326e2d5a081` found that the canonical Scene object model is approaching an extensibility limit.

Current `cad_scene.py` defines a closed taxonomy:

```python
PhysicalEntityKind = Literal[
    'speaker', 'seat', 'screen', 'projector',
    'riser', 'furniture', 'av_equipment'
]
```

and the base `SceneEntity` directly owns type-specific fields:

```text
acoustic_reference_offset_m
speaker_role
aim_xyz
```

with validation such as:

```text
speaker_role is required for speakers
speaker fields are only valid for speakers
```

This was manageable when Scene contained only a small set of physical objects.

However current product plans now require or strongly imply additional semantic physical roles:
- direct-view display (#637);
- tactile actuator (#638);
- theater lighting fixtures/zones (#640);
- rack/cabinet infrastructure (#562);
- treatment placement (#451);
- richer screen/video semantics (#541/#565);
- installed equipment instances (#569);
- Capture semantic handoff with a broader observation taxonomy (#336/#564).

If every new product domain is implemented by:
1. adding another `Literal` kind;
2. adding more nullable fields to `SceneEntity`;
3. adding more `if kind == ...` validation;
4. teaching every consumer about every new kind;

then Scene schema becomes a brittle global switchboard.

## Product risk

This is not primarily a style/refactor concern.

It affects normal product evolution:
- one new object type forces canonical Scene schema migration;
- old/new clients have poor forward-compatibility around unknown kinds;
- generic geometry tools become coupled to domain-specific metadata;
- Capture promotion tends to flatten richer observation types into the nearest available Scene kind;
- one physical object that serves multiple roles becomes awkward.

Example:

A direct-view TV is simultaneously:
- a physical chassis;
- an active image surface;
- an A/V endpoint;
- an installed equipment instance;
- potentially a wall-mounted object.

Encoding all of that as a single increasingly-specialized `kind='display'` record would repeat the same coupling.

## Goal

Refactor Scene semantics toward a **stable physical-object core + typed semantic capability/binding authorities**.

Do not introduce a generic untyped ECS, arbitrary JSON component bag, or plugin framework.

The target is controlled schema extensibility with compile-time/model validation.

## 1. Freeze what belongs in the Scene physical core

A physical Scene object should primarily answer:

> What physical thing occupies this geometry/pose in this SceneRevision?

Stable core fields may include:
- entity ID;
- human name;
- physical geometry/envelope reference;
- pose/orientation;
- lifecycle/source provenance where appropriate;
- physical parent/support relation where canonical.

Do not place every domain's analysis/settings authority directly into the base entity.

## 2. Replace specialization leakage with typed bindings/components

Candidate architecture:

```text
SceneEntity
- entity_id
- physical_kind / geometry class
- name
- pose
- geometry/envelope

SpeakerBinding
- entity_id
- source/topology refs
- installation context

SeatBinding
- entity_id
- seating semantics
- ListenerPose refs

- entity_id
- video aperture/profile refs
- acoustic-screen-transfer ref

DirectViewDisplayBinding
- entity_id
- display specification / installed-instance refs

TactileAttachmentBinding
- actuator/target refs
```

Exact storage shape may be:
- typed discriminated components inside SceneDocument; or
- separate immutable project authorities keyed by SceneEntity ID.

The essential rule is:
> adding a video/tactile/domain capability should not require adding nullable fields to every SceneEntity.

## 3. Avoid one giant `kind` enum as product taxonomy

Keep a small physical classification if useful for rendering/editor affordances, e.g.:
- equipment;
- furniture/support;

- seat-mounted electromechanical excitation;
- tactile-channel routing;
- tactile crossover/gain/delay;
- seat/riser attachment;
- tactile commissioning/verification.

```text
equivalent_monopole_volume_velocity_at_equipment_acoustic_reference
```

A tactile transducer primarily injects **mechanical vibration into a seat/riser/body support**, not acoustic volume velocity into the room.

Representing one as a fake subwoofer/speaker would therefore corrupt both prediction semantics and system topology.

## Product value

Tactile transducers are a common home-theater design option when users want:

- stronger low-frequency sensation without raising room SPL;
- reduced reliance on very high subwoofer output;
- late-night / apartment-friendly experiential bass;
- dedicated seat-row effects;
- tactile augmentation below or around the subwoofer crossover region.

HTDT should be able to document and commission them without pretending to predict body sensation from the room-acoustic solver.

Introduce a bounded **Tactile System** domain that represents:

- physical tactile actuator instances;
- exact attachment/support targets;

- operating filter/gain/delay settings;
- evidence/provenance;
- measured/subjective verification where supported.

Freeze the distinction:

### Acoustic source

Examples:
- speaker;
- subwoofer.

Primary output:
- acoustic radiation into room air.

Authority:
- EquipmentDefinition;
- directivity;
- acoustic reference;
- R110 source/excitation;
- acoustic prediction.

### Tactile actuator

Examples:
- inertial shaker;
- moving-magnet tactile transducer;
- seat/riser actuator.

Primary output:
- mechanical excitation into a support structure.

Do not model tactile actuators as `speaker_role = LFE` speakers merely because they often receive bass/LFE program content.

with distinct reference semantics:

```text
display          -> display_center
projectionScreen -> screen_center
projector        -> projector_body_reference / projector_lens_center
```

HTDT Scene currently has physical kinds:

```text
speaker
seat
screen
projector
riser
furniture
av_equipment
```

but no first-class `display` kind.

The canonical video geometry contract is also projection-specific:

- `VideoGeometryRequest` requires `projector_entity_id`;
- it requires an exact `ProjectorSpecification`;
- `_screen_frame()` only accepts `SceneEntity.kind == "screen"`;
- `_projection_result()` only accepts `SceneEntity.kind == "projector"`.

Therefore a normal TV/OLED/MiniLED/MicroLED/direct-view theater has no clean native digital-twin representation for its video endpoint.

## Why this matters

A Home Theater Digital Twin should support both common architectures:

```text
Projection
source -> AVR/processor -> projector -> passive projection screen

Direct view
source -> AVR/processor -> TV/OLED/direct-view display
```

A direct-view display is not:

- a passive projection screen;
- a projector;
- a generic AV-equipment box with no visible aperture;
- a fake projector placed at zero throw distance.

Forcing it into those types causes semantic loss in:

- physical placement;
- viewing geometry;
- A/V signal-path compatibility (#570);
- HDR/photometric commissioning (#557);
- installation/as-built verification (#520);
- Capture -> HTDT promotion;
- project templates (#614);
- reports.

This is a broad normal-use product gap, especially for living-room / TV-room projects.

## Goal

Add first-class **direct-view display authority and geometry evaluation** while sharing the common viewing/sightline model with projection systems.

Do not fork the entire video stack into unrelated projector and TV implementations.

## 1. Add a direct-view physical entity

Introduce a stable physical scene kind, e.g.:

```text
display
```

representing a physical active-image device such as:

- LCD/LED TV;
- OLED;
- MiniLED;
- MicroLED/direct-view modular display;
- other flat/direct-view panel.

Keep:

```text
screen
```

for a passive projection surface.

Do not infer display vs projection screen from thickness or name.

## 2. Display geometry authority

A direct-view display needs explicit geometry beyond a generic box:

```text
DirectViewDisplayGeometry
- entity_id
- visible_width_m
- visible_height_m
- active_image_center_offset_local_m
- bezel/frame dimensions or clearance
- display normal / facing axis
- optional chassis envelope relation
```

The visible active image area must be distinct from the chassis body.

Reuse the same coordinate/orientation conventions as existing screen geometry.

## 3. Display equipment/specification authority

Do not overload the current loudspeaker-oriented `EquipmentDefinition` with meaningless acoustic fields.

Define or generalize a video-equipment specification authority that can carry:

- manufacturer/model;
- chassis dimensions;
- active-image dimensions;
- supported orientation/mounting;
- video capabilities consumed by #570;
- photometric/HDR capability consumed by #557;
- provenance/version/hash.

Exact naming can be:

- `DirectViewDisplaySpecification`;
- a future typed `VideoEquipmentDefinition`.

The important rule is typed video authority, not one generic JSON equipment blob.

## 4. Installed physical identity

Compose with #569.

The reusable model definition and the installed physical TV are separate:

```text
DirectViewDisplaySpecification
        ↓
InstalledEquipmentInstance
        ↓
Scene display entity / exact pose
```

Serial n

## Summary

Deep playback-chain / calibration / multi-source review of HTDT `main@6ad227fafc88c6f19e0bdda927114326e2d5a081` found a missing system-level authority between channel calibration settings and #492 playback excitation scenarios.

Current calibration authority can persist per-channel:
- gain;
- delay;
- polarity;
- HPF/LPF crossover settings;
- PEQ;
- a generic `routing: tuple[str, ...]`.

#492 correctly plans an exact multi-channel excitation scenario including bass-management routing.

But there is no first-class reusable project authority for the actual home-theater **bass-management configuration** that determines how logical input energy is distributed by frequency across physical speakers/subwoofers.

Repository/current issue search found no explicit model for concepts such as:
- bass-managed vs full-range main channel;
- per-channel crossover policy;
- redirected low-frequency destination(s);
- LFE path and LPF;
- multiple subwoofer output groups;
- duplicated bass / LFE+Main-like behavior;
- frequency-dependent logical-channel → physical-radiator map.

This is a product-level gap because the same configuration must be shared by:
- measurement routing;
- measured-vs-predicted comparison;
- multi-source prediction;
- calibration optimization;
- AVR/DSP application/readback;
- commissioning verification.

## Goal

Introduce a device-neutral, versioned **BassManagementProfile / PlaybackRoutingConfiguration** authority.

It describes the normalized routing/filter semantics of the theater's playback chain.

Vendor-specific terms such as `Small`, `Large`, `LFE+Main`, etc. should be adapter/UI mappings onto this normalized authority, not the canonical semantic model.

## 1. Distinguish three layers

Freeze the boundary:

### A. BassManagementProfile
> What the playback system is configured to do.

Persistent project/device configuration.

### B. MultiChannelExcitationScenario (#492)
> Which logical signals are being played for this prediction/measurement, under an exact playback configuration.

Scenario-specific.

### C. CalibrationPlan / effective applied settings (#452)
> What settings are proposed/exported/applied and later verified.

Lifecycle-specific.

Do not collapse these into one object.

## 2. Normalized channel routing

Represent each logical main channel with semantics such as:

```text
MainChannelBassRule
- logical_role_id
- high_pass?
- redirected_low_band?
- redirected_destinations[]
- transition/filter definition
- source provenance
```

Examples:

```text
C
  HPF 80 Hz LR4
  low band -> SUB1 + SUB2

FL
  full range
  no redirected low band
```

Do not infer routing solely from speaker labels or from the presence of a crossover number.

## 3. LFE path

Represent the LFE signal path independently from redirected bass.

At minimum:
- logical LFE input identity;
- LPF/filter authority if configured;
- gain/trim if this layer owns it, otherwise exact reference to applied settings;
- destination subwoofer outputs/group;
- optional duplication policy where supported.

Do not call redirected main-channel bass “LFE”.

Measured/predicted evidence should preserve that distinction.

## 4. Physical subwoofer groups

Support:
- one sub output driving one physical sub;
- one AVR sub output feeding multiple physical subs through downstream DSP/splitter;
- multiple independently controllable sub outputs;
- external DSP routing.

Model exact physical-source mapping through stable IDs / routing authority.

Do not assume `SUB1` and `SUB2` are independently controllable merely because two subwoofer SceneEntities exist.

## 5. Crossover/filter semantics

Reuse canonical filter/crossover structures where appropriate, but add the missing routing relation.

A main HPF and sub LPF are not enough to establish:
- which main's low band reaches which sub;
- whether full-range mains also remain active below crossover;
- how LFE joins the sub path.

Filter type/order must be explicit when known.

title: Listener pose authority: unify seat ear/eye/head/recline geometry across acoustic prediction, sightlines and measurement targets
body:
## Summary

Deep seat/listener/video-acoustics integration review of HTDT `main@6ad227fafc88c6f19e0bdda927114326e2d5a081` found that the product has two partially overlapping listener-position models but no shared persistent **listener/occupant pose authority**.

Current Scene seat authority:

```text
SceneEntity(kind='seat')
- physical position/orientation/size
- acoustic_reference_offset_m
```

Current video evaluation authority:

```text
SeatGeometryBinding
- eye_reference_offset_local_m
- head_center_offset_local_m
- head_radius_m
- row_id
- riser_entity_id
```

#472 correctly distinguishes:
- physical seat;
- listener acoustic reference;
- measurement point.

But there is still no one versioned project concept for:

> In this seat, where are the listener's ears, eyes and head for the posture we are designing/measuring?

Without that, audio prediction, video sightline and measurement-target generation can use different offsets for what the UI presents as the same listener.

## Goal

Introduce a reusable project-scoped **ListenerPose / SeatOccupancyProfile** bound to a seat.

It should unify the spatial reference used by:
- acoustic receiver evaluation;
- viewing-angle/sightline evaluation;
- measurement target generation;
- commissioning/as-built verification.

It is geometry/planning authority, not personally identifying user data.

## 1. Separate physical seat from listener pose

Keep the seat entity as physical furniture:
- base location;
- dimensions;
- orientation;
- riser/support relation.

Add one or more listener-pose records such as:

```text
ListenerPose
- pose_id / version / semantic hash
- seat_entity_id
- label
- head_center_offset_local_m
- acoustic_reference_offset_local_m
- eye_reference_offset_local_m
- optional left/right ear offsets
- facing/orientation relative to seat
- posture kind
- provenance/source
```

Do not store a person's name, age or other personal identity just to model ear/eye geometry.

## 2. Acoustic reference semantics

Define explicitly what the default acoustic reference means:
- head center;
- midpoint between ears;
- single microphone reference point;
- other declared convention.

Current `acoustic_reference_offset_m` can migrate into the default ListenerPose.

Do not let different solvers silently interpret the same point differently.

## 3. Ear-specific capability

For ordinary room optimization, one head-center/mid-ear reference may be enough.

Where binaural/auralization work later requires it, optionally support:
- left ear point;
- right ear point;
- interaural axis/orientation.

Do not fabricate an HRTF or ear geometry from head radius alone.

#515 auralization can consume ear-specific references only when available.

## 4. Eye/head geometry

`SeatGeometryBinding` should derive eye/head geometry from the selected exact ListenerPose rather than requiring an unrelated manual binding.

This lets #455 sightline answer:
- eye point;
- head obstruction volume;
- row-to-row obstruction;
- screen center elevation angle

from the same posture used for the listener.

## 5. Posture / recline

Home-theater seating commonly has upright and reclined use.

Allow bounded posture semantics:
- upright;
- reclined;
- custom.

A posture may change:
- head/eye height;
- longitudinal head position;
- facing orientation.

Do not rotate the physical seat entity merely because the occupant reclines.

Pose is relative to the seat.

## 6. Multiple planned listener poses per seat

One seat may need more than one scenario:

```text
Seat 1
  Design reference · upright
  Movie posture · reclined
```

One pose is the project's current/default listener reference for normal evaluation.

Variant/study workflows may compare exact alternate poses without rewriting the seat.

## 7. Generic anonymous presets

Optional UX convenience:
- Standard upright;
- Low reclined;
- Custom.

Presets are starting values only.

Do not claim demographic/anthropometric precision unless the source is explicit.

Persist the material

## Summary

Deep Room-CAD productivity review of current HTDT `main@6ad227fafc88c6f19e0bdda927114326e2d5a081` found that editor presentation state is only partially persistent.

`editor_view_states` currently stores:
- selected entity/entities;
- hidden IDs;
- locked IDs.

`RoomViewport3D` itself owns a live VTK/PyVista camera with pan/orbit/zoom/focus/fit behavior, but the repository/view-state contract does not persist:
- camera position/focal point/view-up;
- perspective vs parallel projection;
- zoom/parallel scale;
- active orthographic orientation;
- overlay/visibility combinations;
- user-defined clipping/section state;
- named working views.

#545 correctly tracks canonical top/front/side/elevation editing modes.
#482 correctly tracks entity visibility/lock management.
#578 defines compact viewport display controls.

What is still missing is the operator workflow:

> Save and return to the exact working view I use for front-stage alignment / ceiling speakers / rack / rear treatments.

This becomes a routine productivity issue once the Scene is dense.

## Goal

Add a bounded **Room View Workspace / Named View** layer over the existing viewport.

It is editor/presentation state, not physical Scene truth and not solver authority.

## 1. Persist the last working view

At minimum, reopening a project should restore the last usable Room camera instead of always requiring a new fit/orbit.

Persist a versioned camera record such as:

```text
RoomCameraViewState
- position
- focal_point
- view_up
- projection_kind
- view_angle or parallel_scale
- clipping mode if explicitly user-defined
- updated_at
```

All coordinates use HTDT scene/domain coordinates or an explicitly versioned renderer conversion contract.

Do not persist raw opaque VTK object state.

Allow user-created named views:
- Front stage
- MLP
- Ceiling speakers
- Rear wall
- Equipment rack
- Projector / screen
- Treatment plan.

A named view may bind:
- exact camera;
- projection kind;
- optional visibility/isolation set;
- optional section/clipping state;
- optional selected/focus entity refs.

Saving a view does **not** create a SceneRevision.

Editing/renaming a view does not stale predictions or measurements.

## 3. Built-in canonical views

Compose with #545 rather than duplicating it.

Built-in actions:
- Perspective;
- Top;
- Front;
- Rear;
- Left;
- Right.

#545 remains the authority for orthographic editing/projection semantics.
This issue owns persistence/bookmarks and composing those projections with visibility/section state.
