## Summary

Deep GUI design review of current main 46c31d233997a16ea01573931742e525d76c0343 found that the Measurements workspace has a sound task sequence but still presents analysis through vertically stacked cards rather than one coherent measurement-analysis surface.

Current flow in measurement_page_workspace.py is:

- Import;
- Assignment;
- Quality;
- Comparison.

That workflow is correct.

The remaining GUI problem is composition.

Current Quality page is roughly:

- capability cards;
- 7-column saved-measurement table;
- selected-measurement text block;
- selected-measurement plot.

Current Comparison page is roughly:

- comparison condition card;
- measured/predicted plot;
- difference plot;
- result text block;
- comparison history table.

This is functional, but the operator must repeatedly move attention vertically and mentally reconnect:

- selected measurement;
- target/listener;
- evidence type;
- scene compatibility;
- quality/capability;
- plot;
- comparison history.

This issue defines the **Measurements engineering workspace design**.

#579 owns shared scientific plot grammar.

This issue owns page composition, selection synchronization, tables, analysis hierarchy and task progression.

## Design principle

Measurements should feel like:

> dataset selection + evidence context + analysis result

not:

> a stack of independent cards.

The user should always know which measurement or comparison is currently active.

## 1. Persistent measurement context

Introduce one compact context/header for the active measurement or comparison.

Example:

Selected measurement
FL · Main Listening Position
Measured · Current scene
Quality: usable

or:

Comparison
Measured: FL · MLP
Predicted: FL · MLP
Band: 20 Hz–20 kHz

This context should remain visually tied to the plot/detail.

Do not force users to re-read several table cells after selecting a row.

## 2. Import page

Current import page is already simple.

Refine target composition:

top:
- source choice;
- import action.

main:
- preview plot;
- staged file/measurement summary.

bottom:
- one primary next action:
  "Continue to assignment"

Do not leave the user to infer that the next context tab is Assignment.

### Imported/staged summary

Show:
- source label;
- sample count;
- frequency band;
- available phase/timing capability if known;
- source provenance summary.

Raw filename/path/hash remains Details.

## 3. Assignment page

Current form mixes:
- target;
- evidence type;
- channel role;
- radiation scope;
- routing evidence;
- source speakers.

This is semantically rich but visually flat.

Recompose into sections:

### Measurement identity
- target/listening point;
- channel/input role.

### Evidence class
- measured / predicted / derived / unknown.

### Source / routing
- source speaker(s);
- radiation scope;
- routing evidence.

### Summary
Human sentence:

"Measured Front Left at Main Listening Position using verified single-source routing."

If unknowns exist:

"Routing not verified"

with a clear status.

### Channel role control

Current editable combo includes raw strings such as front_left.

Normal presentation should use localized typed labels:
- Front Left (FL);
- Center (C);
- Front Right (FR);
- Subwoofer (LFE/Sub);
- Unknown.

Raw role token may remain searchable/advanced.

Before committing, present a compact summary.

Example:

Input        Front Left
Evidence     Measured

Routing      Verified

[Save measurement]

This reduces accidental semantic assignment.

Do not add a separate confirmation dialog; the summary is enough for undoable/local work.

## 5. Quality page layout

Target desktop layout:

left/top:
- measurement table/list.

right/bottom:
- selected measurement detail + plot.

measurement list | selected measurement plot/detail

table above plot.

## Summary

Deep product/authority review of current main@6a463b6fa4f4bd85ac3a944938004f6a9cfc80e3 found a missing layer between the digital-twin design state and ordinary day-to-day theater use.

HTDT now has or is planning separate exact authorities for physical SceneRevision/SystemVariant, RoomOperatingState (#556), topology/routing (#505/#473), multi-channel excitation (#492), calibration/applied settings (#452), TargetCurveProfile (#508), video presentation (#565), photometric state (#557), and A/V sync (#560).

Those authorities should remain separate.

What is missing is a versioned operating preset / usage scenario answering:

> Which exact combination of those authorities is the theater actually using for “Movie”, “Music”, “Game”, “Night”, etc.?

Today a user can have all component data while still lacking one reproducible identity for the real operational configuration.

## Why this matters

One physical theater commonly has several valid operating configurations.

Movie may use curtains closed, immersive topology, movie calibration, a reference-oriented target, scope lens-memory, HDR projector mode and a specific HVAC state.

Music may use stereo/2.1, another DSP/listening mode and target.

Game may use low-latency display mode, another A/V sync condition and audio-processing state.

Night may use lower nominal playback level, different low-frequency/dynamic-range policy and a quieter room state.

These are not new SceneRevisions unless physical geometry changed. They should not be free-form notes either.

## Proposed authority

Introduce an immutable/versioned TheaterOperatingPreset / PlaybackOperatingScenario that references existing exact authorities.

Candidate references:

- project/document + physical SceneRevision/SystemVariant;
- RoomOperatingState;
- CurrentSystemTopology / RoutingProfile;
- playback/excitation scenario;
- selected calibration/applied-settings identity;
- TargetCurveProfile;
- listening population / seat priority where relevant;
- VideoPresentationProfile (#565);
- projector/display operating state;
- A/V sync condition;
- intended nominal playback/reference level;
- human-facing purpose/category and provenance.

Do not copy every component value into one giant mutable preset. The preset is an exact composition over existing authorities.

A preset may state intended input/program condition such as stereo PCM, 5.1/7.1 channel-based, object-audio-capable path or game low-latency path.

Do not simulate proprietary Dolby/DTS object rendering unless a separately validated adapter exists.

Where exact decoder/upmixer behavior is unknown, retain declared listening mode/device state plus observed/verified routing and leave unsupported internals UNKNOWN.

- desired preset definition;
- user-confirmed applied device/preset state;
- measured/commissioned evidence under that preset.

Selecting “Movie” in HTDT must not prove the AVR/projector actually switched.

Measurement campaigns should bind the exact preset used so repeated measurements are semantically comparable.

Reports should be able to generate a concise operating-mode summary for the installed theater.

## Summary

Deep static video/acoustics integration review of current main (79262f50777f61e79d12a3be2afdbbb2d5a2680d) found a concrete incomplete slice from closed #175.

HTDT can mark a screen as acoustically transparent = true / false / unknown, but current video-geometry evaluation explicitly returns UNKNOWN for the acoustic effect because there is no acoustic transmission/reflection model.

This is correct fail-closed behavior, but the corresponding acoustic authority/workflow is not tracked by a dedicated issue.

Related: #175, #455, #101, #465, #444, #474, #469

## Current behavior

ScreenGeometryBinding contains geometry, visible aperture, frame clearance and acoustically_transparent.

When the flag is true, cad_video_geometry.py intentionally reports that the screen is marked acoustically transparent but the geometry authority has no acoustic transmission/reflection model, and sets the acoustic-effect state to UNKNOWN.

Source: https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/79262f50777f61e79d12a3be2afdbbb2d5a2680d/backend/src/htdt/cad_video_geometry.py

This is the right semantic boundary.

However, a major practical home-theater configuration remains unsupported: speakers behind an acoustically-transparent screen with a frequency-dependent, angle-dependent screen transfer.

## Why this matters

An AT screen is not acoustically invisible. Depending on screen construction and spacing, it may introduce frequency-dependent insertion loss, high-frequency attenuation, angle-dependent transmission, reflection, phase/delay effects when measured complex data exists, and speaker-to-screen spacing sensitivity.

For a Digital Twin that evaluates speaker placement, directivity and calibration, treating the screen only as AT=yes is insufficient. It would also be unsafe to invent a generic AT-screen correction curve.

## Proposed change

Introduce a first-class immutable AcousticScreenTransfer / ThinTransmissionSurface authority. The exact class name is flexible.

### 1. Separate video and acoustic identity

Keep screen physical/video geometry, visible aperture/aspect/frame, and acoustic transfer model as separate authorities. Changing transfer data must not rewrite projector geometry identity.

### 2. Capability tiers

Allow explicit acoustic capability such as UNKNOWN, metadata-only AT claim, magnitude-only normal-incidence transmission, frequency+angle magnitude transmission, complex transmission with phase, transmission+reflection, and measured validated datasets. Never synthesize phase from magnitude-only data.

### 3. Provenance

Each transfer model should carry manufacturer/measured/literature/inferred/analytic provenance, source asset/document, version/hash, measurement condition, valid frequency range, valid incidence-angle range and uncertainty where known.

A marketing acoustically-transparent label is not equivalent to a measured transfer function.

Transfer data may depend on screen-to-speaker spacing, incidence angle, tension/frame condition, backing layer, source/microphone geometry and normalization. Store applicability explicitly. Outside the valid condition/domain, report LIMITED/UNKNOWN rather than silently extrapolating.

Bind the acoustic transfer authority to an exact screen surface/plane and orientation. Do not convert it into a thick wall volume merely to reuse wall-boundary code.

## Summary

Deep static product/installation review of current main (3e1fb4ebc45db822968b7ca20a8453f37f9c3c54) found that HTDT can export exact Scene XYZ coordinates, but it does not define the **field datum/reference geometry needed to reproduce those coordinates in the physical room**.

The installation output currently declares:

~~~
coordinate_system = htdt-x-right-y-rear-z-up-m
~~~

and exports Scene entity-origin x/y/z, orientation/aim, and top/front/side dimension-sheet points.

That is internally deterministic, but an installer still needs to know:

> From which physical corner/wall/line/height datum do I measure these numbers?

Related: #453, #520, #491, #534, #507, #496

## Current implementation

### Scene coordinate frame

SceneDocument uses one fixed domain convention: htdt-x-right-y-rear-z-up-m.

For legacy/default rectangular rooms, the generated footprint happens to begin at front-left=(0,0), but polygon/manual/imported rooms may use arbitrary world coordinates, and there is no field-survey datum authority that says a specific physical room point is the project origin.

Source:
https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/3e1fb4ebc45db822968b7ca20a8453f37f9c3c54/backend/src/htdt/cad_scene.py

### Installation output

InstallationOutput exports the same world coordinates and orthographic bounds.

InstallationCoordinate stores exact entity XYZ and, for speakers, mounting height explicitly as the Scene entity-origin Z coordinate. The report states that no separate mounting reference is inferred.

Source:
https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/3e1fb4ebc45db822968b7ca20a8453f37f9c3c54/backend/src/htdt/report.py

### Existing UX issues do not define the datum

#453 exposes the existing installation report.
#520 compares proposed vs as-built pose deviations.
#491 adds a ruler.
#534 adds floor-plan underlay alignment.

None defines the stable physical reference from which an installer or commissioning run should measure the exported coordinates.

## Why this is a major specification gap

Exact digital coordinates are not directly actionable unless the coordinate frame is tied to reproducible physical references.

Examples:

- FL X = 1.327 m — measured from which side?
- Y = 0.615 m — from which wall plane?
- Z = 1.050 m — cabinet origin, acoustic center, bracket center, or floor datum?
- after importing Capture/floor-plan evidence, did the project origin move relative to the physical room?
- if a front wall is not square, which line establishes the X axis?
- can a commissioning measurement reproduce the same coordinate frame months later?

Without an explicit datum, installation can be numerically exact in HTDT but still require manual interpretation in the room.

That also weakens #520 commissioning because planned-vs-actual deltas are only trustworthy when both observations resolve into the same exact field frame.

Add a first-class immutable **InstallationDatum / FieldReferenceFrame** authority.

### 1. Explicit physical origin

Allow the user to define a field-reproducible origin from bounded reference types, for example:

- exact room vertex/corner;
- point on a selected wall;
- midpoint of a selected wall;
- screen center/edge where intentionally used;
- explicit surveyed point;
- imported reference point with provenance.

The origin must bind to stable semantic geometry/entity identity where applicable, not only screen pixels.

Define how field X/Y are established, for example:

- selected wall direction = +X;
- perpendicular inward = +Y;
- two explicit surveyed points define +X;
- explicit axis vector.

Do not assume “front wall” unless the user has explicitly established that semantic reference.

Define Z zero/reference independently:

- finished floor plane;
- riser/platform surface;
- explicit survey elevation;
- imported/capture datum where verified.

## Summary

Deep static product/solver-integration review of current `main` (`e8c5ea042b81e0c475e8a42efa8a25a5bfc14d2d`) found that HTDT has the right low-level pieces for multi-receiver prediction, but no first-class native workflow for a common home-theater task:

> calculate and inspect the independent transfer function from each speaker/source to each listening seat/receiver.

This is different from #492 multi-channel coherent playback and from #510 measured multi-seat aggregation.

Related: #457, #492, #510, #475, #478, #101

## Current capability

### Provider can already contain multiple receivers

`LowBandPredictionProvider` is explicitly:

- one exact source identity;
- an ordered set of receiver identities;
- one `LowBandReceiverResponse` per receiver.

`build_r130_low_band_prediction_provider()` currently requires:

- exactly one source;
- one or more receivers.

Source:
https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/e8c5ea042b81e0c475e8a42efa8a25a5bfc14d2d/backend/src/htdt/cad_prediction_provider.py

This is a useful building block for a transfer matrix.

### Product prediction is still one interactive selection

#457 correctly moves Room prediction toward a solver/provider request based on an explicit requested source/receiver/observable/band.

However, no dedicated product contract or UI was found for:

- selecting a set of sources;
- selecting a listening population/receiver set;
- generating all independent source→receiver responses;
- showing completion/cache/capability per cell;
- reusing that exact matrix in later system-level analysis.

## Why this matters

Normal theater diagnosis frequently asks:

- What does FL look like at every seat?
- What does each subwoofer contribute independently at the MLP?
- Which source causes the seat-to-seat variation around 60 Hz?
- Do all channels have comparable response coverage?
- Which exact single-source transfer functions can be reused for a coherent multi-sub scenario?

Manually running:

```text
source 1 × receiver 1
source 1 × receiver 2
...
source N × receiver M
```

is slow and makes it difficult to see missing/stale/incompatible cells.

## Proposed change

Add a solver-neutral immutable **PredictionMatrixSpec / TransferMatrixResultSet** and workflow.

The exact class names are flexible.

### 1. Matrix specification

Pin:

- exact SceneRevision/SystemVariant;
- selected source entities/logical roles;
- exact source/equipment bindings;
- selected receiver/listening population;
- environment authority;
- requested observable(s);
- requested frequency/time band;
- provider/fidelity policy;
- exact source/receiver ordering;
- semantic hash.

The matrix is a set of independent transfer problems, not a playback mix.

### 2. Per-cell exact authority

Each cell must resolve to an exact prediction/provider result:

```text
source A -> receiver 1
source A -> receiver 2
source B -> receiver 1
...
```

Cells may independently be:

- READY / cached;
- queued/running;
- BLOCKED;
- UNSUPPORTED;
- stale;
- failed/cancelled.

Use #478/R140 execution semantics for:

- resource preflight;
- batching;
- cache reuse;
- progress;
- cancellation;
- attempt history.

Where one provider can efficiently solve one source against multiple receivers, exploit that exact batching.

Do not force one solver invocation per visual table cell if the provider supports receiver batching.

## Summary

Deep static optimization/product review of current `main` (`0126ab543a409fce0311622b0772d010bb21304e`) found that HTDT's current multi-seat objective authority is intentionally **equal/unweighted only**.

That is a safe initial implementation, but it is not sufficient for a common home-theater requirement:

> optimize primarily for the Main Listening Position (MLP), while still constraining or accounting for secondary seats.

Related: #472, #510, #140, #142

## Current implementation

`cad_direct_level.py` defines `SeatPopulation` with:

```python
population_weighting: Literal['equal_unweighted'] = 'equal_unweighted'
```

Source:
https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/0126ab543a409fce0311622b0772d010bb21304e/backend/src/htdt/cad_direct_level.py

`cad_coverage.py` similarly fixes:

```python
seat_weighting_semantics: Literal['equal_unweighted']
```

and explicitly requires the coverage scenario weighting to match the receiver population.

Source:
https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/0126ab543a409fce0311622b0772d010bb21304e/backend/src/htdt/cad_coverage.py

Current aggregate objectives therefore emphasize semantics such as:

- worst seat;
- seat-to-seat spread;
- useful coverage fraction;

but do not represent an explicit MLP/secondary-seat priority policy.

## Why this matters

Home-theater optimization often has asymmetric listening importance.

Examples:

- MLP is the reference seat; two side seats are secondary.
- Front row has higher priority than occasional rear seats.
- Every seat must meet a hard minimum, but the MLP should receive tighter FR/target optimization.
- One seat should not dominate a global average merely because all seats are implicitly equal.

The current alternatives are unsatisfactory:

1. optimize only the MLP and ignore secondary seats;
2. include all seats equally even when that does not match user intent;
3. rely only on worst-seat objectives, which encodes a different decision policy from “MLP first, others bounded”.

These semantics should be explicit rather than hidden in objective tuning.

## Proposed change

Introduce a first-class immutable **ListeningPopulation / SeatPriorityProfile** authority.

### 1. Exact population

Bind an explicit ordered set of seat/listener entity IDs to the exact Scene/SystemVariant.

Each member may carry semantics such as:

- primary / MLP;
- secondary;
- optional/diagnostic;

and, where supported, an explicit non-negative weight.

### 2. Separate hard constraints from soft weighting

Do not use a weight to make a required seat disappear.

Support policies such as:

- every required seat must meet minimum target/headroom/coverage;
- among feasible candidates, weighted aggregate favors primary seats;
- worst-seat/spread objectives remain available independently.

This distinction is important: a 0.1 secondary-seat weight must not silently waive a hard minimum.

If numeric weighting is introduced, define it exactly.

For example:

- weights normalized by the evaluator;
- or stored as absolute relative importance and normalized deterministically.

Persist:

- exact member order;
- raw weights;
- normalization algorithm/version;
- required/optional state;
- semantic hash.

Do not infer probability from seat weight.

### 4. MLP convenience

Room/Optimize should allow a normal action such as:

- mark seat as `MLP`;
- create/edit listening population;
- choose “MLP priority + all seats required” preset.

The preset should materialize explicit authority, not remain hidden UI behavior.

### 5. Objective integration

Extend compatible objectives to consume exact population semantics, e.g.:

- weighted FR/shape aggregate;

- combined with independent worst-seat and seat-spread objectives.

Do not collapse everything into one opaque score.

## Summary

Static optimization/product review of current `main` (`0126ab543a409fce0311622b0772d010bb21304e`) found that the normal O10/O80 `CadSearchSpec` supports only independent per-entity XYZ grid axes.

That makes common existing-system optimization awkward or combinatorially expensive because physically linked groups cannot be represented as one search variable.

O100 topology search already has a bounded linked-placement concept for proposed speakers, including `mirror_x`. The generic existing-scene search path does not.

Related: #65, #140, #463, #480, #486

## Current generic SearchSpec

`CadSearchAxis` contains only:

- `entity_id`;
- `axis` = x/y/z;
- min;
- max;
- step.

`CadSearchSpec` is a deterministic Cartesian grid over those independent axes.

Source:
[cad_search_models.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/0126ab543a409fce0311622b0772d010bb21304e/backend/src/htdt/cad_search_models.py)

The workflow-first Optimize UI mirrors that model: choose one entity, one XYZ axis and min/max/step, then add another independent axis.

Source:
[optimization_search_controller.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/0126ab543a409fce0311622b0772d010bb21304e/backend/src/htdt/optimization_search_controller.py)

## Existing linked-search precedent

O100 topology search already supports:

- multiple proposed entities;
- `LinkedPlacementRule`;
- deterministic linked derivation;
- explicit `mirror_x`.

Source:
[cad_topology_search.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/0126ab543a409fce0311622b0772d010bb21304e/backend/src/htdt/cad_topology_search.py)

#463 tracks exposing those semantics for multi-speaker **proposed topology** authoring.

This issue is about the normal as-built/current-scene optimization path.

## Product impact

Common home-theater search variables are often grouped:

- move FL/FR forward/back by the same amount;
- change left/right speaker spacing symmetrically;
- move a complete seat row;
- move two subwoofers as a mirrored pair;
- preserve a fixed offset between paired objects;
- change all height speakers by one common Z offset.

With only independent axes, users must either:

1. search every member independently, producing many physically irrelevant combinations; or
2. optimize one member and manually reproduce the relationship afterward.

Example:

```text
FL X: 11 values
FR X: 11 values
FL Y: 11 values
FR Y: 11 values
```

creates 14,641 Cartesian combinations even if the intended design has only a few hundred meaningful symmetric/group states.

This directly increases compute cost for downstream prediction/robustness and makes the search specification harder to understand.

## Proposed change

Extend generic O10/O80 search with first-class **linked/group search variables**.

### 1. Shared delta

Allow one scalar search variable to apply the same translation delta to multiple entities.

Example:

```text
Seat row Y offset: -0.30 .. +0.30 m
subjects: Seat1, Seat2, Seat3
```

Relative geometry stays fixed.

### 2. Mirrored pair

Allow a pair to be derived around an explicit reference plane/axis.

Initial useful case:

- X mirror about room centerline or a user-selected reference X.

Do not assume the room centerline unless explicitly selected/bound.

### 3. Fixed relative offset

Allow master/slave relation where the slave retains an exact stored offset from the master.

This supports paired speakers/subs that must move together without necessarily being mirrored.

### 4. Group rotation / future orientation

Coordinate with #480 group transforms.

A later extension may support linked yaw/aim variables, but the first implementation can remain translation-only if the identity model leaves room for orientation parameters.

### 5. Deterministic identity

Linked rules must be part of immutable SearchSpec identity:

- relation kind;
- member IDs;
- reference plane/origin;
- fixed offsets;
- variable bounds/step.

- capability availability.

Static review of `measurement_page_workspace.py` found no phase plot.

Source:

## Product impact

Without phase visualization, the user cannot inspect:

- phase trend around crossover;
- relative phase shape between measurements;
- polarity-like phase behavior;
- discontinuities/wrap behavior;
- whether two datasets have visibly different phase response before using calibration/timing tools.

This makes phase capability largely invisible despite the data already being retained.

## Proposed change

Add a capability-aware **Phase Response** view to Measurements.

### 1. Phase plot

For datasets with usable phase samples, display:

- phase vs log frequency;
- wrapped phase by default;
- optional unwrapped view when the unwrapping algorithm/identity is explicit.

Do not mutate the stored original phase samples.

### 2. Separate capability labels

Display independently:

- 位相応答: available/blocked/unknown;
- 共通タイミング: available/blocked/unknown.

A valid phase plot must remain viewable even when common timing is UNKNOWN.

### 3. A/B phase comparison

Extend #483 generic A/B comparison so datasets with phase can optionally show:

- A phase;
- B phase;
- phase difference only when the comparison semantics are valid and explicitly defined.

Do not present absolute/inter-channel delay claims unless common timing is established.

If the UI offers:

- unwrap;
- delay removal;
- excess phase;
- group delay;

each transformation must have an explicit algorithm/parameter identity and be shown as derived presentation/analysis, not original measured evidence.

Initial implementation may limit scope to wrapped/unwrapped phase only.

### 5. Common-timing gate

Absolute timing/delay overlays must consume the exact `common_timing` capability from MeasurementQualityReport.

Never infer timing from the existence of phase samples.

- [ ] native Measurements can plot stored phase samples against frequency.
- [ ] phase response remains viewable when common timing is UNKNOWN.
- [ ] UI visibly distinguishes phase availability from common-timing availability.
- [ ] original phase samples are not modified by display unwrapping.

## Summary

Static product/architecture review of current `main` (`a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566`) found that HTDT's immutable `SceneRevision` lineage is central to measurement/prediction/optimization evidence, but the canonical native product has no first-class revision-history UX.

Users can Save and Undo the current working session, but they cannot normally:

- browse saved SceneRevisions;
- understand what changed between them;
- name/bookmark important design states;
- restore an older design as a new current revision;
- jump from historical evidence to the exact saved scene it references.

Related: #61, #63, #65, #447, #450, #483

## Existing revision authority

`SceneRepository` stores immutable rows with:

- revision ID;
- document ID;
- parent revision ID;
- created timestamp;
- content hash;
- exact SceneDocument payload.

Normal saves enforce a single-head lineage: every new current revision descends from the latest current head.

Source:
[cad_repository.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/cad_repository.py)

This is the correct authority model for reproducible evidence.

## Current product gap

The canonical workflow exposes Save/Undo/Redo and recovery-draft handling, but no revision browser or restore surface.

Therefore immutable revision identity is mostly visible only indirectly through:

- measurement binding;
- prediction staleness;
- SearchSpec;
- SystemVariant;
- validation/provenance.

A normal user cannot answer:

- “Which saved room state did this measurement belong to?”
- “What changed between yesterday's room and today's?”
- “Go back to the layout before I moved the seats.”
- “Open the exact scene used for this prediction.”
- “Mark this state as ‘pre-treatment baseline’.”

## Important semantics

A history feature must **not** mutate or delete historical revisions and should not move the repository head backward.

“Restore revision R5” should mean:

```text
current head R12
+ copy physical Scene content from R5
→ create new revision R13 with parent R12
→ provenance says restored-from R5
```

Existing evidence remains bound to its original revision IDs/hashes.

## Proposed change

Add a first-class **Scene History** surface.

### 1. Revision list

Expose saved revisions with human-readable information:

- timestamp;
- optional user label/note;
- broad change summary;
- whether current head;
- references from measurements/predictions/SystemVariants where useful.

Avoid making raw UUIDs the primary UI.

### 2. Named checkpoints

Allow a user to add a label/note such as:

- baseline;
- before treatment;
- final speaker placement;
- as-built survey.

Labels should be metadata over immutable revision identity, not edits to historical Scene content.

### 3. Diff

For two revisions show structured differences such as:

- room geometry changed;
- entity added/removed;
- position/orientation changed;
- equipment/role changed;
- acoustic/material/treatment authority changed where applicable.

Do not reduce the diff to a single “changed” flag.

### 4. Historical preview

Allow read-only 3D preview of an old revision and optionally ghost/current overlay.

Historical preview must never be mistaken for the active editable Scene.

### 5. Restore-as-new

Provide explicit:

`この状態を現在の設計として復元`

which creates a new revision from the latest head using old scene content.

Never reassign existing measurement/prediction evidence to the restored copy.

### 6. Evidence deep links

From Measurements / Prediction / Optimize, “測定時の部屋を表示” or equivalent should open the exact bound revision in history preview.

## Repository support

If needed, add a canonical list/history query to `SceneRepository` rather than having UI code directly query SQLite.

History metadata/labels should have an explicit persistence authority separate from immutable Scene content if labels must be editable.

## Acceptance

- [ ] native UI can list saved SceneR

## Summary

Static product/UX review of current `main` (`a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566`) found that the canonical Measurements comparison UI does not expose comparison controls already supported by the comparison authority:

- reference band for level alignment;
- excluded frequency bands.

As a result, the UI cannot properly separate **absolute level difference** from **response-shape difference**, even though the saved comparison model includes `level_offset_db` and `shape_rms_db`.

Related: #316, #483, #452, #468

## Existing comparison authority

`compare_frequency_responses(...)` accepts:

- requested comparison band;
- optional `reference_band_hz`;
- `excluded_bands`.

When a reference band is supplied it computes:

- mean level offset over the valid reference grid;
- shape RMS after subtracting that offset.

It also removes excluded bands from the valid grid.

Source:
[comparison.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/comparison.py)

`CadMeasurementComparison` persists:

- `reference_band_hz`;
- `excluded_bands`;
- `level_offset_db`;
- `shape_rms_db`.

Source:
[cad_measurement_models.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/cad_measurement_models.py)

## Current workflow limitation

`MeasurementWorkflowController.compare_datasets()` only accepts:

- low_hz;
- high_hz.

It calls `compare_frequency_responses()` without reference/exclusion arguments.

Source:
[measurement_workflow.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/measurement_workflow.py)

Measurements > 比較 likewise exposes only lower/upper frequency limits.

Source:
[measurement_page_workspace.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/measurement_page_workspace.py)

The result UI still shows a `形状RMS` field, but the normal native path cannot request the reference-band calculation required to populate that metric meaningfully.

## Why this matters

For acoustic A/B interpretation, these are different questions:

- Is one response globally louder?
- Does the spectral shape differ after level alignment?
- Is a narrow invalid/noisy band dominating the RMS?
- Did calibration improve smoothness while changing reference level?
- Are two seats similar except for one known unsupported band?

A single raw RMS over the whole requested band cannot answer all of them.

## Proposed change

Extend the generic comparison UX from #483 with explicit comparison-spec controls.

### Reference band

Optional user-selectable reference band used only for level alignment / shape comparison.

The UI must state:

> reference band affects level-offset/shape metrics; it does not modify the original stored data.

Useful presets may include:

- none;
- user-defined;
- common acoustic bands only if clearly labelled as convenience presets.

### Excluded bands

Allow one or more explicitly listed excluded ranges.

Each exclusion should show the reason when user-entered, e.g.:

- known measurement artifact;
- unsupported range;

```text
measured dataset  vs  predicted dataset
```

That UI limitation blocks several normal measurement workflows already implied by retake, calibration, multi-seat and as-built validation features.

Related: #172, #316, #452, #468, #472

Measurements > 比較 is titled:

- one 予測 combo.

The refresh logic explicitly filters:


## Summary

Static UX/architecture review of current `main` (`a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566`) found that the workflow-first Room workspace effectively regresses the multi-selection/group-editing semantics previously specified and implemented under N20b / #49.

The persisted view state can still carry multiple selected IDs, but the canonical Room interaction/controller path collapses normal selection to one entity and all primary edit actions operate only on `selected_id`.

Related: #49, #55, #118, #464, #470

## Current canonical behavior

`RoomWorkspaceController.set_selection(entity_id)` does one of only two things:

- clear selection; or
- `set_selection((entity_id,), primary_id=entity_id)`.

It never adds/removes members from the current ordered selection.

Source:
[room_workspace.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/room_workspace.py)

The Room viewport exposes a single:

```python
entitySelected = Signal(object)
```

and a picked actor simply emits one entity ID. There is no modifier/multi-select intent in this canonical signal path.

Source:
[room_viewport.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/room_viewport.py)

Room actions such as:

- duplicate;
- fit selection;
- Inspector edit;
- transform controller start;

resolve through `controller.selected_id`, not the full ordered selection.

## Prior required semantics

N20b / #49 explicitly requires:

- ordered multi-selection with a primary entity;
- Ctrl add/remove in tree/viewport;
- common-pivot group Move/Rotate;
- relative geometry preservation;
- one group drag = one Undo;
- clear behavior when locked entities are included.

Those requirements are still important for the current product.

## Why this matters

A realistic theater contains repeated/grouped objects:

- left/right or surround speaker pairs;
- 3–8 seats;
- seat rows;
- multiple treatment panels;
- racks/components;
- furniture groups.

Without multi-select, common edits become repetitive and error-prone:

- move a whole seat row 120 mm;
- raise all height speakers;
- rotate a pair consistently;
- duplicate three seats together;
- compare/align several objects.

This also makes proposed future richer object geometry (#464) significantly harder to use.

## Proposed change

Restore first-class multi-selection in the workflow-first Room UI using the existing ordered selection model.

### 1. Selection interaction

Support:

- click = replace selection;
- Ctrl-click = add/remove;
- optional Shift range selection in object list/tree where meaningful;
- empty-space click = clear;
- primary selection remains explicit.

Viewport and object list must reflect the same selection set.

### 2. Group transform

Move/Rotate selected editable entities using a common pivot while preserving pair/group relative geometry.

Do not independently snap every member in a way that deforms the group.

One gesture = one atomic command / one Undo.

### 3. Locked objects

If selection contains locked/non-editable entities, define one explicit rule:

- reject group edit with explanation; or
- edit only the clearly indicated editable subset.

Do not silently partially transform an ambiguous set.

### 4. Multi-selection Inspector

For common properties:

- show shared value when equal;
- show mixed state when different;
- permit deliberate batch update for appropriate fields.

Do not expose fields that cannot safely be batch-edited.

### 5. Duplicate / align utilities

At minimum, group duplication should preserve relative arrangement.

Alignment/distribution can remain a later enhancement unless already supported by existing CAD semantics.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Ctrl-click in viewport can build/remove an ordered multi-selection.
- [ ] Room object list and viewport selection stay synchronized.
- [ ] primary selection remains visually distinct.

## Summary

Static architecture/product review of current `main` (`a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566`) found a mismatch between the legacy Room prediction input and the R-series acoustic environment contract.

The current native prediction panel lets the user enter an ad-hoc sound speed with a default of 343 m/s. The R-series AcousticSceneSnapshot deliberately requires an explicit environment authority and source provenance for sound speed/temperature instead of synthesizing defaults.

Related: #101, #394, #457, #471, #140

## Current native prediction input

`RoomPredictionPanel` contains:

```text
音速: 343.00 m/s
```

with a numeric range and no source/provenance concept.

The value is submitted as a run parameter.

Source:
[room_prediction.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/room_prediction.py)

This was reasonable for a simple N70 geometry model but should not become the final R-series product environment authority.

## R-series contract

`SnapshotEnvironmentAuthorityRef` explicitly stores:

- exact external environment authority;
- optional sound speed;
- exact source authority for sound speed;
- optional temperature;
- exact source authority for temperature.

Value and source must be supplied together.

Source:
[cad_acoustic_snapshot.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/cad_acoustic_snapshot.py)

#394 separately tracks stronger read-side resolution of those external refs; this issue is about **user/product authoring and lifecycle**.

## Why this matters

Sound speed affects:

- mode frequencies;
- propagation time/phase;
- wave/geometric solver consistency;
- measured-vs-predicted timing;
- later environment uncertainty analysis.

A bare 343 m/s form value does not say whether it is:

- a standard nominal assumption;
- derived from measured room temperature;
- manually measured/entered;
- copied from a previous session;
- applicable to the current measurement campaign.

Likewise, prediction and measurement under materially different environment conditions should not be presented as exactly comparable without stating the difference.

## Proposed change

Add a first-class **Acoustic Environment Profile** and integrate it with Room prediction and Measurements acquisition context.

### 1. Environment profile

At minimum support:

- sound speed;
- temperature;
- provenance/source kind;
- captured/effective timestamp;
- optional notes.

Future-compatible fields may include humidity/pressure only when a model actually consumes them.

Do not collect irrelevant environmental fields merely for completeness.

### 2. Explicit source semantics

Examples:

- `Nominal standard assumption: 343 m/s`;
- `Derived from measured temperature: 21.5 °C`;
- `Manual measured sound speed`;
- `Unknown`.

A nominal assumption is allowed but must be labelled as an assumption, not a measurement.

### 3. Persisted selection

Room > 音響 should select an exact environment profile/version for a prediction request.

Do not silently create an exact source authority from the numeric spinbox.

### 4. Measurement linkage

AcquisitionContext should optionally bind the environment profile used at measurement time.

Prediction-vs-measurement views can then show:

- same/compatible environment;
- different environment;
- unknown.

### 5. O90 integration

Environment uncertainty can later reference the same authority/profile model rather than introducing a separate temperature/sound-speed vocabulary.

## Acceptance

- [ ] normal prediction can bind an explicit environment profile instead of a provenance-free sound-speed scalar.
- [ ] 343 m/s nominal assumption remains available but is visibly labelled as an assumption.
- [ ] sound-speed/temperature values carry exact source/provenance as required by AcousticSceneSnapshot.
- [ ] changing an environment profile/version can stale/recompu

## Summary

Static product/spec review of current `main` (`a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566`) found that the generic helper `acoustic_reference_position(entity)` is being used as a proxy for **receiver eligibility** even though the same reference is also the **source acoustic reference** for speakers.

As a result, normal prediction and measurement-target pickers can expose source speakers as receiver/measurement locations.

Related: #472, #470, #169, #457, #471

## Current semantics

`SceneEntity` has one optional `acoustic_reference_offset_m`.

`acoustic_reference_position()` returns:

- a measurement point's own position;
- or the transformed acoustic-reference offset of any physical entity that has one.

Source:
[cad_scene.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/cad_scene.py)

New speakers are created with an acoustic-reference offset, as they should be for source modeling.

New seats also carry a reference offset, representing a listener/ear reference.

## Current consumers

### Room prediction

`RoomPredictionController.receiver_options()` includes every entity satisfying:

```python
acoustic_reference_position(entity) is not None
```

Therefore speakers are valid entries in the UI's “受音点” selector.

Source:
[room_prediction.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/room_prediction.py)

### Measurement assignment

`MeasurementWorkflowController.assignment_targets()` uses the same test.

Therefore a speaker can also appear under “測定位置”.

Source:
[measurement_workflow.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/a597c66b4f5902381f370ce6f24ca56bfb737566/backend/src/htdt/measurement_workflow.py)

## Why this is a specification problem

“Has an acoustic reference point” does not mean “can act as every acoustic role”.

Examples:

- speaker acoustic center/reference = valid source reference;
- seat ear position = valid listener/receiver reference;
- microphone point = valid measurement receiver;
- screen acoustic reference, if added later, would not automatically be a receiver;
- source/receiver coincidence may be a specialized simulation case, not a normal product selection.

Using one helper as a capability predicate collapses distinct semantics.

It also creates confusing UI behavior: selecting a speaker in Room can cause prediction UI to prefer that selected entity as the receiver.

## Proposed change

Introduce explicit acoustic-role/reference semantics rather than inferring capabilities from non-null coordinates.

### 1. Separate reference concepts

At minimum distinguish:

- source acoustic reference;
- listener/receiver reference;
- measurement/capsule reference.

These may share a physical location/transform implementation but must not share capability semantics implicitly.

### 2. Explicit receiver eligibility

Normal product receiver pickers should be based on declared consumer semantics, for example:

- Room product prediction:
  - seat/listener reference;
  - explicit measurement point;
- Measurement assignment:
  - explicit measurement point;
  - seat-derived target only through the binding semantics of #472.

A speaker should not appear unless a specialized workflow explicitly requests source-as-receiver evaluation.

### 3. Solver-neutral request contract

Prediction/provider requests should identify receiver semantics, not only an entity ID and derived position.

This avoids later ambiguity when R-series supports:

- point receiver;
- measured receiver authority;
- seat population;
- spatial receiver/field.

### 4. UI labels

Pickers should say what the target represents:

- `MLP seat · ear reference`
- `Measurement point 1 · microphone position`

rather than presenting all acoustic-reference-bearing entities equivalently.

## Acceptance

- [ ] default Room prediction receiver picker does not list source speakers.

## Summary

HTDT implements versioned StandardsProfile authority and native Standards evaluation, including a `user_defined` profile kind, but the native workflow only seeds/selects/evaluates profiles. There is no user-facing way to create or version a user-defined profile.

This leaves part of closed Issue #170's stated scope unreachable from the product UI.

Related: #170, #418, #118, #142

## Current behavior

`StandardsWorkspaceModel` seeds built-in source authorities/profiles and exposes read/evaluate operations.

The UI:

- lists profiles;
- labels them as built-in or user-defined;
- evaluates the selected profile;
- shows criterion provenance;
- lets the user explicitly opt criteria into hard-constraint behavior.

- [standards_workspace.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/standards_workspace.py)

However it has no native action to:

- create a user-defined profile;
- clone a built-in profile as a user profile;
- add/remove criteria;
- define required inputs and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN semantics;
- record source/reference provenance;
- publish a new immutable profile version;
- import/export a profile.

Issue #170 explicitly included **user-defined profiles** in scope and is currently closed.

## Why this matters

Home-theater layouts often need project-specific constraints that are not identical to one published standard.

Examples:

- user-chosen viewing-angle bounds;
- custom speaker clearance;
- installation-specific height/angle ranges;
- local constraints derived from an architect/installer document;
- a conservative subset of published guidance;
- a new version of the same criteria after requirements change.

Without a native editor, the data model advertises flexibility that ordinary users cannot use.

## Proposed change

### Standards library

Add a library/editor surface, preferably reachable from Room > placement/Standards and Settings:

- Built-in profiles: read-only
- User profiles: create/version/archive
- Clone built-in → user-defined draft
- Import/export exact profile JSON

### Criterion editor

For each criterion expose:

- user-facing name/description
- metric/input domain
- operator/range
- unit
- required inputs/capabilities
- applicability conditions
- source/reference/evidence note
- whether the criterion may be explicitly selected as a hard constraint

Do not allow a user-defined profile to overwrite a built-in profile/version.

### Immutable versioning

Editing a published profile must create a new version.

Existing saved evaluations remain bound to the old exact profile version/hash.

### Safety semantics

The editor must preserve existing semantics:

- PASS
- FAIL
- UNKNOWN
- NOT_APPLICABLE

Missing input must not be coerced to PASS or FAIL.

A criterion must not become a hard constraint unless the user explicitly opts it in at evaluation/use time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Native UI can create a user-defined StandardsProfile without scripts/DB edits.
- [ ] A built-in profile can be cloned into a new user-defined identity without mutating the built-in authority.
- [ ] User can add/edit/remove criteria with unit/operator/required-input/source metadata.
- [ ] Saving changes to a published user profile creates a new immutable version.
- [ ] Existing evaluations remain reproducible against the old exact version.
- [ ] Import/export preserves semantic identity/provenance and rejects malformed/unknown required fields.
- [ ] UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE behavior is previewable before publishing.
- [ ] Hard-constraint use remains explicit and profile-version-specific.

## Summary

HTDT already contains a rich InstallationOutput v3 authority and deterministic CSV/HTML rendering, but the canonical native UI does not expose report generation/export.

Issue #176 is closed, so this is a product-surface completion issue rather than a request to redesign the report backend.

Related: #176, #420, #422, #171, #173, #175

## Existing implementation

`report.py` already contains InstallationOutput v3 with:

- exact SceneRevision/SystemVariant binding
- installation-facing entity coordinates/orientation
- top/front/side dimension-sheet data
- projector/screen summary
- StandardsProfile summary
- AcousticTreatment placement/quantity summary
- CalibrationPlan requested/exported settings summary
- deterministic CSV rendering
- self-contained HTML report rendering

- [report.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/report.py)

Focused repository tests also exist for installation reports/authority integration.

Yet the workflow-first native surfaces do not call:

- `build_installation_output`
- `render_installation_csv`
- `render_installation_report_html`

in the normal Overview / Room / Measurements / Optimize composition.

## Impact

The app can compute/store install-relevant authority but does not give the user a normal “take this design into the room” handoff.

That forces manual transcription of:

- speaker coordinates
- height/yaw/pitch/aim
- projector/screen geometry
- treatment dimensions/quantity
- calibration settings
- standards/validation status

Manual transcription is exactly what #176 intended to eliminate.

## Proposed change

### 1. Installation/Report action

Expose a first-class action from a context where the exact design is explicit, e.g.:

- Overview: `施工・設定資料を作成`
- Optimize comparison: `この構成の施工資料…`

Do not generate from an ambiguous “latest” variant when multiple alternatives exist.

### 2. Pre-export completeness review

Before export show:

- selected SceneRevision
- selected SystemVariant / lifecycle
- sections AVAILABLE / UNKNOWN / NOT_APPLICABLE
- stale evidence warnings
- treatment/calibration/projector/standards availability
- measurement/validation status

UNKNOWN sections should remain visible as unknown, not silently disappear.

### 3. Preview

Provide a readable preview of:

- coordinates
- orthographic dimension sheets
- equipment/treatment summary
- calibration settings
- standards/validation evidence summary

Internal UUID/SHA can remain under Advanced/provenance.

### 4. Export

At minimum expose existing deterministic outputs:

- CSV
- HTML

Optional PDF can initially use platform print-to-PDF from the HTML view; it does not need a second report authority.

### 5. Lifecycle semantics

Generating a report must not imply:

- proposal is installed;
- calibration was applied;
- measured is validated;
- missing evidence is PASS.

The report is a view of exact stored authority only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can select an exact SceneRevision/SystemVariant and open installation-output preview.
- [ ] Ambiguous current/proposed/as-built alternatives require explicit selection.
- [ ] Section completeness and UNKNOWN states are visible before export.
- [ ] Exported CSV is byte-deterministic for the same InstallationOutput authority.
- [ ] Exported HTML embeds the exact semantic payload and provenance.
- [ ] Coordinates/settings shown in preview equal the exported authority.
- [ ] Report generation does not mutate scene/lifecycle/evidence state.
- [ ] No manual spreadsheet transcription is required for supported coordinate/settings fields.
- [ ] Missing treatment/calibration/projector/standards evidence is represented explicitly.
- [ ] Happy path requires no browser legacy UI, API calls or scripts.

body:
## Summary

HTDT has a substantial CalibrationPlan authority, export format, verification MeasurementPlan and append-only lifecycle implementation, but the canonical native workflow does not expose them to users.

Issue #173 is closed, yet the implemented capability is currently backend-only from the normal workflow-first UI.

Related: #173, #172, #174, #176, #358, #354

## Existing authority

`cad_calibration.py` already defines:

- `CadCalibrationPlan`
- capability-gated support evaluation
- channel gain/delay/polarity/crossover/PEQ
- target curve
- generic biquad export
- deterministic JSON/CSV rendering
- exported/quantized settings snapshot
- `CadVerificationMeasurementPlan`
- lifecycle states:
  - proposed
  - exported
  - user_applied
  - remeasured
  - validated

- [cad_calibration.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/cad_calibration.py)

Persistence and lifecycle checks exist in:

- [cad_calibration_repository.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/cad_calibration_repository.py)

InstallationOutput v3 can report requested/exported calibration settings.

However the canonical native workflow files do not import or expose CalibrationPlan actions:

- [measurement_page_workspace.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/measurement_page_workspace.py)
- [optimization_workflow_workspace.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/optimization_workflow_workspace.py)
- [workflow_application.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/workflow_application.py)

## Product impact

The digital-twin lifecycle currently reaches:

```text
measure / validate / optimize
→ backend can build calibration authority
→ native user has no workflow to use it
```

This leaves a major gap between analysis and actual AVR/DSP setup.

A user should not need Python/repository calls to turn an accepted design and measurement into explicit settings, apply them externally, and verify them by re-measurement.

## Proposed native workflow

### 1. Build CalibrationPlan

From Measurements > comparison/quality or Optimize > measurement/validation:

- choose the exact eligible measurement / dataset;
- show the exact MeasurementQuality capability gates;
- choose target curve / supported channel scope;
- show equipment/device capability limits;
- build a plan only for supported claims.

Unavailable phase/common-timing capability must disable corresponding delay/all-pass operations.

### 2. Review requested settings

Show per channel:

- gain
- delay/distance representation
- polarity
- crossover
- ordered PEQ
- target curve
- headroom/safety notes
- unsupported settings with reasons

### 3. Export

Expose existing deterministic adapters:

- generic JSON
- generic CSV

Show requested settings vs quantized/exported settings before download/save.

Export must not imply the user applied settings.

### 4. Explicit user-applied transition

Add an explicit action such as:

`実機へ設定したことを記録…`

with confirmation of:

- exact export identity;
- device/sample-rate context;
- any manual deviations.

Do not auto-promote on file export.

### 5. Verification measurement loop

After user-applied:

- build the exact `CadVerificationMeasurementPlan`;
- deep-link to Measurements;
- show required points/channels/conditions;
- bind new evidence only when it matches the preregistered plan;
- compare before/after;
- keep remeasured and validated as separate states.

### 6. Overview status

Surface concise lifecycle status:

- calibration proposal available
- exported, not yet confirmed applied
- applied, verification measurement required
- remeasured, validation pending

- 概要

- 測定
- 最適化

## Impact

Today an installed-user happy path is effectively:

```text
launch HTDT
→ implicit/default document
→ all work happens there
```

- multi-room use is not discoverable;
- a user cannot clearly tell which project is open from the shell;
- backup/restore scope is harder to understand;
- synthetic/demo and real projects can be confused if data directories are reused;

- current project name
- New project

一方、SceneRevisionは強い履歴authorityですが、Undo/historyは「意思決定のために残す案」と同義ではありません。

実際にはユーザーは例えば以下を比較したいです。

- Current
- Seat 20 cm forward
- FL/FR toe-in変更
- Treatment A
- Treatment B
- Candidate 07を適用した状態
- As-built
- Measured state

これらを「過去revision番号を覚える」「各workspaceの比較を別々に再構成する」方法ではなく、一つのnamed comparison setとして固定したいです。

`docs/COMPETITIVE_PRODUCT_RESEARCH_2026-09-19.md` でも named design variants / comparison sets はhigh-priority gapとして挙げられています。

immutableな **DesignComparisonSet / DecisionSet** を追加し、既存authorityへのexact refsだけを保持する。

```text
Comparison Set: "Seat / treatment decision"

A  Current

   prediction ...
   measurement ...
   standards ...

B  Seat 20 cm forward
   SceneRevision ...
   prediction ...
   robustness ...

C  Treatment A
   SceneRevision / treatment authority ...
```

### Keep separate from

- Undo/Redo history
- optimizer candidate set
- O100 topology comparison
- measurement A/B

- user-facing name / note

- created timestamp/provenance

- 「過去の比較セットを開く」

を提供する。

- どのevidenceがあるか

title: Measurement ingestion UX: batch campaign import, idempotent duplicate handling, and source attachments
body:
## Summary

current `main` (`7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11`) のnative Measurementsは、single-file / single-pending importを中心に実装されています。

これは基本動作としては成立していますが、home-theaterの実測campaign（複数speaker × 複数seat × repeats）では操作量と誤割当リスクが大きく、`docs/MEASUREMENT_WORKFLOW.md` に既に記載されているimport contractにも届いていません。

Related: #172, #166

## Current implementation

`MeasurementPageWorkspace.import_rew_text_dialog()` は `QFileDialog.getOpenFileName()` で1ファイルだけ選択します。

`MeasurementWorkflowController` も:

```python
self._pending: PendingMeasurementImport | None
```

という単一pending stateです。

- [measurement_page_workspace.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/measurement_page_workspace.py)
- [measurement_workflow.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/measurement_workflow.py)

REW APIも一覧から一件選んでsnapshotをstageするworkflowです。

## Existing specification already expects more

[MEASUREMENT_WORKFLOW.md](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/docs/MEASUREMENT_WORKFLOW.md) は既に以下を要求しています。

- 複数ファイルは各ファイルの成否を表示
- 成功したものだけを明示的に保存可能
- 失敗分を再実行しても成功済みmeasurementを重複登録しない
- same raw bytes と same acquisition / different export を区別
- same acquisitionの別exportを別Datasetとして関連付け可能
- filename / REW UUID / hashだけで自動統合しない
- .mdat / calibration file / setting notes等のsource attachmentsを保持

現在のone-pending UIでは、campaign規模が増えたときこの契約を実用的に満たせません。

## Why this matters

実際のcampaignでは例えば:

- FL/FR/C/SL/SR…
- MLP + secondary seats
- repeat measurements
- calibration / holdout

があり、数十measurementを順番に一件ずつ:

```text
選択 → 読み込み → 割り当て → 保存
```

するのは、時間だけでなくchannel/point取り違えの主要因になります。

これは性能最適化より先に、実測evidenceを正しく集めるためのproduct reliability/UX問題です。

## Proposed change

### Batch staging queue

Import contextに複数pending itemを持つqueue/tableを追加する。

表示例:

- source filename / REW title
- parse status
- frequency band / phase status
- proposed channel
- proposed measurement point
- duplicate/re-export status
- attachment status
- commit status / error

### Assignment template

複数itemへ:

- common measurement point
- evidence type
- AcquisitionContext
- source mapping pattern

を一括適用し、個別override可能にする。

filenameからの推定はproposalに留め、自動確定しない。

### Idempotent duplicate/re-export resolution

少なくともUIで以下を分離する。

1. exact same raw bytes already imported
2. same REW/acquisition identityだが別export
3. same conditionsに見えるが別取得
4. genuinely new measurement

automatic mergeではなく、既存Measurement再利用 / new Dataset / new Measurement を選択させる。

### Source attachments

batch/campaignに:

- REW .mdat
- microphone calibration file
- settings/notes
- optional other raw source

を添付し、既存RawAsset/backup authorityへ保存する。

## Acceptance

- [ ] 10件以上のREW text filesを一度にstageできる。
- [ ] 各itemのparse/assignment/error状態を保存前に一覧できる。
- [ ] common assignmentをbulk applyしつつ、itemごとにoverrideできる。
- [ ] 一部失敗しても成功itemだけ明示的にcommitできる。
- [ ] retryで既にcommit済みitemを重複登録しない。
- [ ] exact duplicate / same-acquisition re-export / new acquisitionを区別して解決できる。
- [ ] raw source attachmentsをproject backupへ含む既存authorityに保存できる。
- [ ] file name / UUID / hash一つだけでmeasurement identityを自動確定しない。
- [ ] single-file workflowも簡単なケースとして残す。

- Review type: static product/spec/UX review

を別状態で維持する。

## Summary

2026-09-21 の current `main` (`7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11`) を静的レビューしたところ、workflow-first shellの入口である Overview が、現在のHTDTのauthority breadthに追従できていません。

これはレアケースの不具合ではなく、日常的な「次に何をすべきか」の情報設計上のgapです。

Related: #118, #142, #166

## Current behavior

`OverviewReadinessService` は各 notice に `OverviewAction` を保持しています。

- measurement missing → 「REWを読み込む」
- phase/timing unavailable → 「測定品質を確認」
- prediction stale/missing → 「予測を実行 / 再計算」
- validation blocked → 「検証を確認」

しかし native Overview の card renderer は notice の `message` しか描画しておらず、card固有の action を捨てています。

- [overview_readiness.py](https://github.com/bolph71656-ai/Home-Theater-Digital-Twin/blob/7898fa2ff4c4794ade3b7cd5563bac796dcefe11/backend/src/htdt/overview_readiness.py)

画面上で直接実行できるのは、priorityで一つに畳まれた `next_action` のボタンだけです。

そのため、複数のwarning/blockerが同時にある場合、ユーザーは問題自体は見えても、該当workspaceへ自力で探しに行く必要があります。

## Larger specification mismatch

Overviewのread modelが現在集約するのは概ね:

- latest SceneRevision
- generic measurement
- prediction
- search spec
- model validation

です。

一方、現在の製品authorityには既に以下があります。

- EquipmentDefinition / source capability
- StandardsProfile / criterion evaluation
- O90 robustness
- SystemVariant proposed / applied / as-built / measured
- SystemVariant-specific MeasurementPlan / Campaign
- treatment / installation output / calibration等の後続authority

`docs/COMPETITIVE_PRODUCT_RESEARCH_2026-09-19.md` 自身も、Overviewは lifecycle 全体のreadinessへ拡張すべきとしています。

現状は「Overview = 次の作業」という #118 の設計原則に対して、実装済みauthorityの増加にUIが追従していません。

## Proposed change

Overviewを機能一覧や総合scoreにはせず、**actionable lifecycle dashboard**として拡張する。

1. 各 blocker / warning card が自身の `OverviewAction` を直接表示する。
2. 一つの primary `next_action` は残すが、他のactionを隠さない。
3. 現在のprojectでrelevantなstageだけを表示する。
   - Room / source readiness
   - Prediction
   - Measurement / quality
   - Optimization / robustness
   - active SystemVariant lifecycle
   - validation
4. SystemVariantが存在する場合は少なくとも以下を区別する。
   - 提案のみ
   - SceneRevisionへ適用済みだが未設置
   - as-built
   - measurement plan不足
   - campaign preregistered
   - evidence incomplete
   - measured / validation pending
5. unavailable / unknown / stale を「完了」へ潰さない。
6. internal UUID/SHAを通常表示へ出さず、既存deep-linkを使う。
7. hidden overall score / automatic winnerは作らない。

## Acceptance

- [ ] warning/blockerが2件以上同時に存在しても、それぞれのcardから該当workspaceへ直接遷移できる。
- [ ] measurement warningがprimary next actionでなくても「REWを読み込む」「測定品質を確認」へ到達できる。

body:
## Finding

The Capture -> HTDT ingestion boundary now preserves more than raw mesh geometry, but most of that information is not yet connected to normal HTDT scene authoring.

HTDT-Capture v1 entities can carry, among other things:

- speaker/subwoofer/display/screen/listening-position/seat/reference-point identity;
- exact `coordinate_space_id` and `T_world_from_annotation`;
- speaker orientation and channel role;
- acoustic-center authority;
- versioned HTDT `equipment_ref` with semantic SHA-256;
- placement method and evidence references.

Capture measurements can retain quantity, value/unit, endpoints, acquisition method, uncertainty, attestation and provenance.

The reference ingestor converts annotations/measurements into deterministic authority handoffs, and HTDT persists those records. Raw and postprocessed RoomPlan evidence is also retained.

However, current Capture semantic promotion is intentionally mesh-centric: it resolves a `RawVisualMesh`, requires an explicit Capture-world -> scene alignment, accepts manually supplied `SurfaceSemanticAssignment` values, and produces semantic geometry. It does not surface the imported annotation/measurement/RoomPlan authorities as typed authoring inputs to the normal scene workflow.

The current promotion document explicitly lists automatic mapping from Capture annotations/RoomPlan objects into surface semantics as deferred work.

## Impact

- Operators can capture speaker/listener placement and equipment identity on iPhone, then be forced to re-enter the same information in HTDT.
- Re-entry can lose the exact Capture evidence/handoff identity and coordinate authority.
- User-attested measurements can remain stored but disconnected from geometry/scene reconciliation.
- RoomPlan/annotation evidence is preserved for audit but underused as a guided authoring source.

## Proposed change

Add a provenance-preserving **authoring handoff** after Capture ingestion.

This should not silently promote Capture inference into final acoustic truth.

The handoff should:

- expose imported annotation, measurement and RoomPlan records grouped by Capture ingestion/revision;
- resolve exact record locators back to immutable source evidence;
- require explicit `coordinate_space_id` alignment before spatial records enter an HTDT scene;
- offer compatible speaker/subwoofer/listener/display/reference-point records as scene-authoring candidates;
- verify any `equipment_ref` against HTDT's versioned equipment authority before use;
- expose user-attested measurements to a reconciliation workflow rather than overwriting mesh/RoomPlan geometry;
- expose RoomPlan categories/objects as suggestions where useful, not as automatic solver semantics;
- preserve Capture source-evidence IDs, handoff IDs, payload hashes and alignment authority in downstream SceneRevision provenance;
- surface conflicts between Capture authorities instead of resolving them invisibly;
- require an explicit operator action before mutating a SceneRevision.

## Acceptance criteria

- After importing a Capture bundle, HTDT can enumerate its typed annotation/measurement/RoomPlan authoring inputs without parsing raw DB JSON manually.
- Spatial candidates cannot be applied without a matching explicit Capture-world -> scene alignment authority.
- A compatible equipment reference resolves by exact definition/version/semantic hash; stale or unknown references are reported rather than silently substituted.
- Applying selected Capture entities preserves their exact source/handoff provenance into the resulting SceneRevision lineage.
- Conflicting user-attested / RoomPlan / mesh-derived information remains separately queryable and is surfaced to the operator.
- No Capture-derived object or RoomPlan class becomes solver-ready semantic authority merely because it was imported.
- No RDC is required for the backend/domain slice.

## Related

- HTDT-Capture #5
- HTDT-Capture #7
- HTDT #101
- HTDT #118
- HTDT #167

title: Capture ingestion: enforce immutable capture_revision identity and parent/series topology
body:
## Finding

Capture Bundle v1 defines `capture_revision_id` as immutable:

> A finalized `capture_revision_id` never mutates.

Corrections are expected to create a new revision under the same `capture_series_id`, with `parent_revision_id` naming the prior revision when applicable.

HTDT's current production ingestion boundary validates UUID shape and deterministic ingestion lineage, but its persisted ingestion identity is keyed by `lineage_digest`.

Current `capture_ingestion_runs` persistence stores:

- `lineage_digest` as the primary key;
- `bundle_digest`;
- `capture_revision_id`;
- ingestor identity/configuration;
- full `plan_json`.

It does **not** persist/index `capture_series_id` or `parent_revision_id` as revision-topology authority, and `capture_revision_id` is not unique.

As a result, two separately valid plans can currently reuse the same `capture_revision_id` with different bundle content, series identity, or parent identity, as long as they produce different ingestion lineage digests.

That violates the Capture-side immutable revision identity contract at the untrusted backend boundary.

This is distinct from HTDT-Capture #144, which addresses producer-side self-parent validation. HTDT must independently enforce the received revision contract.

## Important distinction

A capture revision and an ingestion run are not the same identity.

The same immutable Capture revision may legitimately be reprocessed later by a newer supported ingestion implementation and therefore have more than one ingestion-run identity.

The invariant needed here is:

`capture_revision_id -> exact Capture bundle identity`

not:

`capture_revision_id -> one forever-fixed ingestion lineage digest`.

## Proposed change

Add an explicit persisted Capture revision registry/topology authority keyed by `capture_revision_id`.

At minimum retain and enforce:

- `capture_revision_id`;
- `capture_series_id`;
- `parent_revision_id`;
- exact `bundle_digest`;
- capture schema/version.

On ingestion:

- if a revision ID is new, register its immutable bundle identity;
- if it already exists, require the same bundle digest/series/parent/schema identity or fail closed;
- reject self-parenting independently of producer validation;
- when a parent is already known, require it to belong to the same capture series;
- define an explicit policy for out-of-order parent arrival rather than silently treating absence as valid topology;
- prevent cycles as enough topology becomes known;
- link one or more supported ingestion runs to the immutable Capture revision.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two different bundle digests cannot be registered under the same `capture_revision_id`.
- A reused revision ID with a different series or parent is rejected.
- Self-parent is rejected by HTDT even if producer validation regresses.
- Known parent/child revisions must belong to the same capture series.
- Out-of-order child import has a documented, queryable state/policy and is reconciled when the parent appears.
- Reprocessing the exact same immutable Capture revision under a newer supported ingestion implementation remains representable without changing the revision identity.
- Existing consistent ingestion records migrate without identity loss; any pre-existing conflict is surfaced rather than guessed.
- No RDC is required.

## Related

- HTDT-Capture #144
- HTDT-Capture #7
- HTDT #101
- HTDT #167

Static review only. No implementation performed. RDC not used.

title: Capture integration contract: add cross-repository compatibility CI against pinned HTDT-Capture fixtures
body:
## Finding

The Capture ingestion contract is currently verified independently in the two repositories, but there is no CI check that exercises the **actual same contract artifact end-to-end**.

Current HTDT-Capture `main` (`0b976b98245bcc40a36e34755370130627b7ac4c`) owns the reference contract and frozen Phase 6 fixture:

- `samples/phase6-integration`
- Capture Bundle / ingestion-plan schemas
- `tools/htdt_ingestion/reference_ingestor.py`
- frozen bundle digest:
  `925108a1b3c1b432182efe1b7e18ccb0f1d98f4f17c939ca66a6095b0cc28550`
- frozen lineage digest:
  `729a7590fb1d1e2142c196187ef11a9078522326daa1ef2fd2364b8fd1ef6bf1`

HTDT `main` (`9e6066259ec58c093e9a7587550ccf907f28402f`) independently duplicates/pins the corresponding model and identity semantics in `capture_ingestion_transaction.py`, including the reference-ingestor name/version, hash domains and exact configuration digest.

Its focused tests construct their own plan/payload fixtures rather than consuming the frozen HTDT-Capture integration fixture.

Therefore both repositories can remain green while drifting incompatibly.

## Risk

Contract drift can occur in any of these without being caught across the boundary:

- schema fields or required values;
- provenance vocabulary;
- deterministic ID domain strings;
- reference-ingestor version/configuration digest;
- source-ref semantics;
- record locators;
- mesh handoff fields;
- canonical JSON behavior;
- frozen lineage output.

That failure would be discovered only when a real Capture export reaches HTDT.

## Proposed change

Establish a pinned cross-repository compatibility gate.

Preferred shape:

1. publish or pin an immutable HTDT-Capture contract revision (tag/release artifact or exact commit);
2. make HTDT CI obtain the schemas, frozen fixture and canonical reference-ingestor output from that immutable revision;
3. build/validate the real ingestion plan and feed it through HTDT's production `CaptureIngestionPlan` + `CaptureIngestionRepository` path;
4. verify the frozen bundle/lineage identities and exact authority linkage;
5. fail closed on any contract mismatch;
6. require an explicit pin/version update when the contract intentionally changes.

Do not use floating HTDT-Capture `main` as the sole compatibility authority. A separate non-blocking canary against latest `main` can be added if useful.

## Acceptance criteria

- HTDT CI consumes an immutable, versioned HTDT-Capture contract fixture rather than only a locally reconstructed equivalent.
- The frozen Phase 6 bundle passes through the production HTDT plan validation and ingestion boundary.
- Intentional changes to schema/version/domain/configuration require an explicit compatibility update.
- An incompatible Capture-side contract change causes the HTDT compatibility gate to fail deterministically.
- A compatible implementation-only Capture change does not require arbitrary digest churn.
- The pinned source revision is recorded in CI output/artifacts for auditability.
- No RDC is required.

## Related

- HTDT-Capture #7
- HTDT-Capture #135
- HTDT-Capture #146
- HTDT #101
- HTDT #167
